author: Keel (brief 010, 2026-10-15)
rule: Every event the city simulation runs: what it needs, what it charges, what it changes and who sees it (GDD §11: events carry conditions, effects, witnesses). Anything not in this file or in people.rules.json is rejected (§01: unknown = reject). Scales, temperaments, needs, ties, the Talker test, knowledge and the reference approach prices are read from people.rules.json through p: refs and condition kinds, never restated here. Every number lives once in `values`, tagged as the GDD tags it: [B] built and proven in the top-down test, [S] starting value to tune by playtest, [L] later; a value or rule the GDD does not decide carries proposed: true and a reason, for Sky. Conditions are keyed by `k`, effects by `do`, always the first key, so the C# engine reads them as tagged unions. Outcomes are tried in order and the first whose conditions all hold applies; the last has none, so every event resolves to exactly one outcome. `also` entries apply after the outcome, in order.

reads: scales: min, max and named steps; every move clamps to them
temperaments: respondsTo, refuses and reportsApproach decide an approach's fit; start values
approaches: requires, usd, timeS and trail are the base price line of each Turn event
needs.list: metBy (which approach acts on a need), requires (what a replacement need may need)
knowledge: needsKnown positions (K9), identity face only, learnedBy witnessed or told
tiers: only the simulated carry memory and can be questioned (Sky Q5)

tags.B: built: proven in the top-down test (~/Projects/the-suborned/testbed/reference/suborned-world-sim.cjs) or stated [B] in the GDD
tags.S: spec: a starting value the GDD states [S], tuned by playtest

units.s: integer seconds; the engine steps at 10 Hz (§11), so 1 s = 10 ticks
units.standing: district standing, integer: above 0 Hero, below 0 Menace
units.orders: orders of the same approach to the same person
units.hops: ties crossed by one piece of news
units.per-mille: integer weight scale for seeded draws
units.pct-points: integer points added to a shot's per cent, signed

worse-pressure-trail.reason: Pressure costs no money, so its step is +1 T (a louder threat), in one order. A second threat instead would add a second +1 resentment and make an Informer of anyone not Fearful (resentment max 2): a cliff, not a step.

rivals-retreat-s.reason: Brief 059 (engine 0.32.0): the crew is five people; when more than half of it on the map is down before the final fight it breaks, leaves in its car for this long and comes back with whoever is still up (it was the single crew gun's two hits).

rivals-block-m.reason: The block point (routine.arrive): the first point of the stand's exit lane at least this far from the cell's car. On the Handover's square it is Rocket Lane 10 m from the car (94.5 m from the turn-in, stopping about 2:56); at the service drive the drive's mouth on Apron Road (16.7 m). Far enough that the rival car never stands on the cell's car, near enough that its footprint lies on the way out.

mislead-rival-s.reason: A misled member watches the place he was sent to this long, then walks back. The lookout to the target's other door (about 22 s each way): away from his post about 104 s, so on the Handover the word covers Popovic's car leaving (5:53) only if it lands between about 4:16 and 5:52. The card says when he is back.

rivals-pay-usd.reason: Paid to walk away, not to act: under half the driver's $70,000. Help Lukac $40,000 + $30,000 fits the purse; Pay Lukac $70,000 + $30,000 is all of it. A Mercenary takes it; a Loyal man refuses and the money stays with the cell.

rivals-pay-s.reason: As a Pay on anyone (pay-s), the conversation's length.

rivals-pay-trail.reason: As a Pay on anyone: a payment is traceable money (+2 T), charged when it is taken.

rivals-temper-max-pct.reason: No temperament over 60 % of the crew (the people rules' restricted rule, §04): of five, at most three of one kind.

unclaimed-hold-s.reason: The search's 60 s at a scene (§05 bodies): a shooting is unclaimed only if no operative is in the response's sight when it arrives or while it holds the scene this long.

unclaimed-scene-m.reason: V2 (b): the police look at who is still near the scene, not at everyone on the map. 30 m: about the square. With the break about 8.5 s after the disable, a holster and a 30 m walk (about 19 s at 1.6 m/s), the cell has to be clear in about 30 s against a response arriving 35-45 s after the first shot: tight, seed-dependent, earnable.

split-police-s.src: Motive briefs/096/motive/misses.html, misses.json (Sky 2026-11-05: all recommended); engine 0.43.0; was 60 (Motive's lend addendum, 2026-11-05)
split-police-s.reason: L8 (Motive's misses page L8-police). Sky 082.1: 'police coming until done ... if they're not in the car'. One clock, shown from vale.out. Measured on quiet-b: the crew breaks a median 26.5 s after vale.out and our car leaves about 20 s later; at 60 s, 40 of 200 seeds lost all three to the police. At 75 s (with the late Go before 8:05) all four out 69.5 % of wins, 0.52 captured a win. 90 s buys nothing: vale.out is about 6:49, so the 8:10 close caps the clock at about 81 s.

fight-loud-officers.reason: §07 gives the range; the low end is the base, and only violence raises it (fight-loud-alert, fight-loud-civilian), so the count says how loud the run was.

fight-loud-alert.reason: +1 officer when Alert reached 3 (lockdown): the city sends more to a run a civilian saw.

fight-loud-civilian.reason: +1 officer when a civilian was shot: the fourth officer is the price of the ugliest run.

fight-warn-s.src: §07 safe: helped Inez warns 10 s early

fight-ambush-m.reason: the ambush springs when the Enforcer brings Vale within 20 m of the getaway car: close enough that the car is the bait, far enough that the Enforcer can't just step in.

fight-hold-m.src: Sky 2026-10-18, brief 018 the getaway (Motive), option 3: "get my team into the car, and get away"; was 25 m (§07 final fight [S]: always)
fight-hold-m.reason: a hostile within 8 m reaches a door in 5 s at the rivals' 1.6 m/s, about pistol point blank (5 m) plus a car's width. The ambush and police stops (12–19 m) stand outside it, so the car is held by those who come for it, not by the fight around it.

fight-block-m.src: Sky 2026-10-18, brief 018 the getaway (Motive), option 3: "get my team into the car, and get away"
fight-block-m.reason: the stretch a car needs to pull out of a kerb bay and reach speed (about 4 s at 3.5 m/s²); a body in it is in the car's way. The exit lane is this much of the getaway route's carriageway ahead of the car (site getaway.exit).

fight-block-near-m.reason: beyond fight-hold-m (8 m) and point-blank (5 m): the blocker holds the lane, not the door, and the cell's cover works against it. Also the open post: the lane centreline this far from its start when no cover stands in the ring

fight-block-far-m.reason: inside pistol-eff-m (15 m) by 2 m: the cell at the car and the blocker are in each other's effective reach, so the fight starts and Go is never a standoff

fight-blockers.src: Sky 2026-10-18, brief 018 the getaway (Motive), option 3: "get my team into the car, and get away"
fight-blockers.reason: one hostile per fight goes for the road. It doesn't pass on, so the car is freed by downing one, not all.

investigators-base.src: §05 investigators [S][L]: count rises with A and T
investigators-base.reason: one investigator works any open Trail; the count is what the debrief reads, so it says how hard the city looks.

investigators-per-alert.src: §05 investigators: count rises with A and T
investigators-per-alert.reason: +1 investigator for each Alert level the mission reached: a lockdown sends four.

investigator-hops.src: §05 investigators: ~60–90 s per hop; useful answer → go there, question again
investigator-hops.reason: each investigator follows two leads before the next mission (a hop is one person questioned, §05's 60–90 s, and the debrief reads the result). Two hops are one step up the chain and one more: the Talker who saw the Fixer, then whoever stood where that Talker points.

carry-s.reason: lifting a downed operative takes 3 s; then the carrier walks only and doesn't fire (§06 downed: carry or captured).

gunfire-trail.src: Sky-approved fights, Motive addendum 2026-10-15 (briefs/011/motive-fights.md, Addendum) Q1; §02 Trail: gunfire is a traceable act
gunfire-trail.reason: a shooting is a case: the first shot at each target costs +2 T, hit or miss (shots heard on a civic square open a file); the final fight stays untraced. Loud goes to 9 T, above Pressure (8).

draw-incident-s.src: Sky-approved fights, Motive addendum 2026-10-15 (briefs/011/motive-fights.md, Addendum) Q1: drawn weapons at one place are one incident
draw-incident-s.reason: Keel: the cell drawing on one order, or one beat apart (c003: the Scout and the Fixer 0.9 s apart), is one sight; a second draw 5 s or more later, or beyond witness range of the first, is a new act. Place is the witness range (witness-range-m).

lover-stay-s.reason: one value for every lover in every mission; the mission reads it, never restates it.

summon-walk-max-s.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door §1.4
summon-walk-max-s.reason: keeps a summons local, about one block (≤ 126 m at 1.4 m/s); the Handover's walk fits; bounds the absence at ≤ 4 min, so no generated mission gets an endless lure.

summon-alert-max.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door §1.4
summon-alert-max.reason: he answers through an inquiry (Alert 1) but not a search (Alert 2: security staff stay at their posts): the lure is for a quiet run.

summon-pressed-stay-s.src: brief 085, Motive pressure-guard.md §1; Sky approved the rule: a pressured Inez warns the guard and he runs back to his door
summon-pressed-stay-s.reason: she has to tell him, and the player has to see him hear it; his run back is the response unit's existing pace (security.speed), not the cell's, because guards move slow

standing.rule: One integer per district, starting at `start` (one step short of the Hero band: Sky 2026-10-16, 'Hero is kinda the default'). At or above `hero` the district is in the Hero band, at or below `menace` in the Menace band, otherwise neutral. In a mission only acts seen or found move it: each witnessed incident of a Hero act adds one `step`, of a Menace act takes one (traceable[].standing, witness.sees), a public fight moves it once when it ends, by whom the cell fought (fight.public, Sky 2026-10-16: 'it should be per fight, and depends who you're fighting'; not capped, and a move for the drift), and a found killing moves it takedown.foundKillStanding; a missing person moves nothing. Facts along ties never move it (Sky Q6). Between missions the word does (standing.word): each person the cell helped, pressured or knocked out this mission, alive, not missing and with a tie of a kind in `word.ties`, tells those ties how a stranger treated them, once per person, not per tie: helped +`word.step`, pressured or knocked out −`word.step`; a person both helped and harmed counts as harmed (a threat outweighs a kindness). The word's net move in a district is clamped to ±`word.cap` a mission; seen and found acts are never capped. The word is a feeling, not a fact: no face, place or time and nothing about the cell goes with it, so it is no fact for word.passes, the Talker test or the investigators, and word-quiet-loyalty does not stop it. Then (standing.drift) a district where nothing moved Standing this mission (no act seen or found, in the mission or after it, and no word) moves `drift` back toward `start`, from either side, never past it. The debrief carries one Standing line per district (debrief.lines.standing) with its cause, one of `causes`: the cause that moved it most toward the net change (the earliest on a tie), `balanced` when the moves cancel, a drift, or `steady`. Heat (§06) = campaign Trail + max(0, −standing), unchanged: from the start it takes 3 net Menace steps before Standing adds Heat, and Hero never cancels Trail; its threshold is Motive's.

alert.rule: An incident is one act at one place and time; every shot of one fight with one target is one incident. Any gunfire raises Alert to at least `gunfire` (§05's own rule; Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md retires §06's +1 A a shot), and calls the response unit. Violence seen by a civilian sets violenceSeen at once. Alert never falls within a mission.

memory.rule: A memory entry is {act, by, place, time, witnessed} (Motive K1). `by` is the face of the operative who did the act: a face is only an id (Adams 2017), and only the Fixer's face is a fact (people.rules talker.facts; §03 the face witnesses remember), so an entry whose `by` is a key of faceFacts also yields that fact. `witnessed` = a third person saw the act. Only a `remember` change writes memory, only acts listed here, only on simulated people (people.rules tiers; Sky Q5). A told entry carries the fact it was told and is never retold (one hop). The facts a person holds are the union over their entries; people.rules talker.lie's `helped` is an entry of act `help`; a remembered refusal is an entry of act `refusal`. An entry yields its act's facts as listed here, plus the face fact of `by` (faceFacts). camera.rule: Bribes on camera (engine 0.40.0). A Pay or a Pressure (`approaches`) is recorded when a live camera (not looped, not cut, not shot out; Game.CameraWatching, the test the watchers' log and attention use: in a head's cone, a clear line from its lens to the head or chest, no crowd across it) watches the Fixer or the person being turned at any tick of the act (`window`), from its start in place to its end or its cancel. One act is one record and one incident, however many cameras see it; the first camera to see it is the record's. The record lands at that camera's desk's next scan at or after the first watched tick (`report.scan`, phase from the camera's id, as attention and witness.cameraScan) plus `report.call`: then the act costs `trail` Trail (on top of the approach's own), it is an incident (the nth raises Alert to at least alert.byIncident[n-1], and to at least `alert`: a found fault), the dial dispatches its response to the subject's place (an alarm with no body), and the investigators get a lead: the place and time, the person approached, and the Fixer's face when a live camera watched him at any tick of the act (`lead`). No Standing (`standing`): the desk is security, not the public. On tape: a loop, a cut or a shot after the watched tick does not undo it, and a camera's record lands though nobody is at the screen. A record still to land when the mission ends is charged at the end (Trail, the lead; no Alert). Ask, Listen and Help are never recorded: they stay private (rulebook privacy). The Pay and Pressure cards say it before the commit (Quote.Recorded*): the camera that would see the act where it is done ("?" for a camera the cell has not watched), the Trail, the Alert and the seconds to its landing, and the loop's end when a loop runs out during the act. Logged camera.recorded (made) and camera.record-lands (landed).

privacy.rule: A turning conversation is private (Sky 2026-10-16), with one exception since engine 0.40.0: a live camera records a Pay or a Pressure it watches (rulebook camera); Ask, Listen and Help stay private to every watcher. An event marked private (Listen, Ask, Pay, Help) has no witnesses: onlookers within witness range learn nothing from it, so it makes no witness fact or memory, no witness Trail, no Standing move, no incident for the investigators, nothing told along ties and no word between missions, and its card counts nobody who would see it. The event's own price stands: its base Trail (Pay is still traceable money), its time and cash, and the subject's own memory and report (a Loyal person still reports an approach). Pressure is not private: a threat is visible, and onlookers see it, remember it and pass it on (witness.sees). Every event by the Fixer or the Scout says whether it is private; a private event may carry no witnesses. Watch is no conversation (not private) and no traceable act (no witnesses): watching someone shows nothing. The traceable acts payment and debt-cleared stay in `traceable` for a visible act that is not a conversation; no turning verb makes them now. Engine 0.28.0: the private approaches are witness.notice.never: nobody notices them at any Alert. Pressure (the traceable act threat) is witness.notice.odd (brief 054 §8, Sky 2026-10-25: confirmed): security see it at every Alert, ordinary people only from people-care-alert; below it a threat at a café table is nobody else's business.

seen.rule: Who sees an Enter and what it does (GDD §07 fail line; engine 0.34.2). The Enter is checked when it starts, the Enforcer at the public door (S.GuardPost): the door guard at his door (not lured, not down) sees it and the mission fails entry-seen-guard (Vale is warned); else the live entrance camera (not looped, not disabled, not blocked) sees it and it fails entry-seen-camera (the Office locks down). The patrol robot is no fail (`patrol` report): if its sight (its sweep cone at its eye, or on an alarm where it walks and holds; not rerouted, not down) holds the door, the Enter goes on and the robot radios what it saw, a seen act reported as attention reports a loiterer: it lands attention.report.call s later (by radio) as a found fault, Alert to at least attention.alert, no Trail, no Standing, a sighting (watcher patrol, the Enforcer, the door), and the dial's dispatch to the door, once per incident; one such report a mission; a patrol downed before it lands drops it. Its attention clock on the Enforcer holds through the Enter as through any act (attention.rule). The response's officers and robots who see an Enter do nothing beyond their clocks (unchanged). `patrol` fail (or no `seen`, a rulebook pinned before 0.34.2): the patrol's sight fails entry-seen-patrol, as before.

driveCar.rule: The getaway car's Drive (brief 059 K6; GDD v0.25.0 §07 getaway; Sky's answer 1a). An operative in the getaway car orders it to one of the mission's car stands (site getaway.stands: the square's bay where it starts, the service drive behind Vale's car). It drives the drive grid at car.pace; everyone in the car rides, busy until it arrives (agent-busy); the car's position, its exit lane, the fight's ambush spots and police stands, Board and the seats are the current stand's. Price: $0, 0 T, no Alert, the drive's seconds (Motive M059-2.1). Refused while the car is held (drive-held, brief 018), with nobody of the cell aboard giving it (drive-no-driver), while anyone in the car is mid-act (drive-busy), for an id that is no stand (unknown-stand), for the stand it is at (drive-here), and once the final fight has started (drive-fight, Motive M059-2.2: the fight is fought at the stand where it started; Go is the only way out). Refused too while a standing car is on the car's way out (drive-boxed, after drive-held) and while one is on the way out of the stand it would drive to (stand-boxed: it can't get in), each naming the car in the way (car.box, engine 0.40.0). A car on the service drive, or driving there, when Vale's car would turn in takes it: the turned driver pulls in at the kerb short of the drive (car.kerb) and the hand-off happens there; his car never boxes the cell's.

listen.rule: A discreet Listen, for anyone on any mission (brief 085, Sky). Given out of place, the agent walks to a spot rather than to the person. Someone with a known walk: read ahead `look` s every `step` s and take the earliest moment the agent can already stand in place, then a free chair within reach and no nearer than `nearWalking` if one comes up within `chairGrace` s, else the nearest free ground beside something solid on a clear line; always out of every watcher's cone, read at the choice. A chair is free if no walker's stop holds it through the act and `chairMargin`. Someone who stays put: the same choice now, no nearer than `nearStill`. An agent already within reach, no nearer than `nearStill` and beside something solid is in place and stays. Nothing found: the plain walk in, stopping at reach. The agent waits at the spot (within `atSpot`) up to `hold` s from the choice, then chooses afresh; waiting holds the attention clock, as an act does. The person holds still for the Listen as rounds.holds says, keeping their own facing. Costs nothing and draws nothing: the Listen stays private.

approach.rule: A person act given out of reach is taken, not refused (Sky 2026-10-22): Watch on a person, Listen, and the four approaches (Ask, Pay, Help, Pressure). The order is checked as when given in reach (the person on the street and not down, the event's needs other than reach, cash for the worst case, the driver's last chance with the walk counted), then the operative walks the grid toward the person at a walk (cell.speed), aimed at where the person will be when the operative gets there (a server's round, read ahead; anyone else where they stand), re-aimed every `repath` s and whenever the walk ends. The act starts on the first tick the operative stands within the event's reach (and, for a Watch, has a clear line): it is checked again then exactly as an order given there, and if refused then (the person gone off the street or down, a need lost, cash spent) it is dropped with that refusal and nothing is charged. From its start the act is what it always was: it takes its time, a server stands still while spoken to (rounds.holds). Nothing is paid and nothing held before the start. The walk in is a walk: seen and noticed as any walk is. Any other order given to the operative (a move, another act, a fire order) or a cancel ends the walk in; a stance, a draw, a holster or a cease does not. No walk to the person: refused no-walk. A driven operative is never walked (cell.drive): out of reach it is refused too-far as before. walkIn false (or no approach section, a rulebook pinned before engine 0.23.0): out of reach is too-far, as before.

drive.rule: EXPERIMENTAL (brief 025). A driven agent is moved by the host (a character controller) and handed to the engine as drive samples, one an operative a tick at most, each an order in the log: {do: drive, to: [x, y] cm, run: true for Shift, face: degrees} and {do: drive, release: true}. The first sample takes control: a walk in progress ends (kept for a resume on release). Each tick the engine moves the agent toward its sample: at most its distance budget (refilled each tick by the pace it may move at: cell.speed, or cell.runSpeed for a run, a carrier's walk while carrying, cell.speed while a run is refused as a move's run is; held at `burst` ticks of it) plus `slack`; then over the walk grid one axis at a time (x, then y), each stopped at the first blocked cell, so it slides along walls and never crosses one; then a step that would end within `gap` of a person on the street and nearer than they were is not taken (an axis alone is tried). The engine's position is the agent's: the host reads it back. Everything else reads the agent where it stands (sight, witnesses, reach, Vale beside the Enforcer). A run is one span, from the first run sample to a walk sample or release, however its heading turns: running is noticed as a move's run is (attention.run; its sighting once a span), and a run ends a fire order. A busy agent (an act in progress): onBusy `cancel`: pushing it `busyPush` in all cancels the act at the cancel line's cost (rulebook cancel); `hold`: it stands until the act lands. Down, inside, in the car or carried, control ends. A click move ends control; acts given while driven are taken where the agent stands (no walk to reach). Release: onRelease `stand`: the agent stands where left; `resume`: the walk control took over goes on from here. A playground start may set pace (per mille of every pace), onBusy, onRelease and gap (Start.drive), hashed with the start state.

cell.rule: The cell's verbs other than Turn, Watch and Listen (§03): how long each takes, how near the operative must stand, the Trail it leaves. An act on a device or a door (Loop and Reroute at the cabinet, Enter at the public door, Board at the getaway car) is done at it, within `atReach`; acts on people keep `reach` (Sky 2026-10-15 playtest). Carry: an operative lifts a downed one in `carry`, then walks only and doesn't fire. Board and Go (brief 018, Sky 2026-10-18): Board is an order on the getaway car, given within `atReach` of it, not running, not mid-action, not carrying a body; it takes `board.s`, and `carry.s` more when carrying (the carried go in first: Vale, only the Enforcer carries him, or a downed operative). An operative in the car is off the street and doesn't fire, and is a target as one still beside cover (weapons.mod.cover); a move on a boarded operative steps out at the car's side in `board.s`, then walks; Vale stays in. Go, given by anyone once someone is in the car, is refused while the car is held (fight.hold) and names the holders, and with nobody standing in it (car-no-driver: a downed operative can't drive; engine 0.34.0, Motive M067-K3 c); the car leaves at once with whoever is inside and the mission ends. The win is Vale in the car when it leaves; Go without him is the cell withdrawing by car. Left behind at Go: a downed operative not in the car is captured (why downed); a standing one is captured if a combatant is still up and not broken (fighting) or the seal clock runs (sealed), else walks out and is back next mission (walked). Captures happen only at Go; a failed mission and the menu's Withdraw capture nobody. Seen leaving: a police officer, a robot or an engaged patrol up and with the car in its cone or within witness range on a clear line (a final-fight officer: a clear line within weapons.pistol.max, brief 018 §10) makes the departure one witnessed incident (witness-trail) and gives the investigation the car (cell-car, a hunted car next mission); rivals don't report. No auto-board: standing at the car is not boarding. An order takes its time and lands at its end; a Call lands at once (the top-down test's spill: the guard walks from the call). Running (Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md): a move with run at runSpeed; refused while carrying Vale or a downed operative, or while doing an action; only security notices a runner (Sky 2026-10-22: "running only in front of camera, patrol bots and guards get you noticed, anyone else fine"; police officers count as security, Sky via Aster 2026-10-22): security staff on the street within witness range on a clear line (the door guard, a job in witness.staff) remember where and when (and the Fixer's face), and a security watcher that sees it (a live camera, the guard by his cone, the patrol, the response's robots and police officers, and a security-staff person on the street other than the door guard, not turned, who sees it by the guard's sight rule: his facing cone (perception.facing, the way he walks) with the near sense, on a clear line, people blocking, and at a stop the near sense only; Sky via Aster 2026-10-22, "a guard is a guard") logs the sighting once per run (run.seen) and, if it keeps a clock, counts the run on it (attention.run; engine 0.34.0, brief 067, Motive M067-B2: a run is seen and suspicious, never a found fault on its own; runAlert is retired); anyone else (passers-by, staff of the shops and the Office who are not security, Inez, the driver, Vale) doesn't notice a run, and the rival crew never did. Running is free while a fight is on. Enter takes enter.alarm longer once Alert ≥ 2 (the staff hide Vale). Loop: the cabinet loops one camera at a time, one of `loop.targets` (a camera of the site by id, or `world`: the city's own cameras, the Records Square mast); the pickup camera joined the list on Sky's answer 6 (2026-10-16: "if the tech takes out the camera, then taking out the guard and driver is possible"; Waymark, briefs/013/waymark-handover.md §5.1). Loop v2 (brief 058 §2, engine 0.31.0; Sky 2026-10-25: a loop runs 2:00): the Tech splices the loop at the cabinet in `loop.s`, it lands (+`loop.trail`) and plays on its own for `loop.run` seconds from the landing, wherever the Tech goes, then the live feed returns (log loop.ends); no tether: he may run, Watch, board and walk off. One loop at a time: a Loop on another camera while one runs is refused loop-holds, with the tick it ends; looping the camera already looping re-splices it, charges `loop.trail` again and runs a fresh `loop.run` from the new landing (no stacking). A Loop on a dead camera (shot or cut) is refused camera-dead. Disable (brief 058 §2; Sky 2026-10-25: Disable is an incident): the Tech, at the cabinet, cuts a camera's line in `disable.s` (`disable.targets`: the cameras the cabinet loops); when it lands (+`disable.trail`) the camera is dead for the rest of the mission (recorded as cut, not shot), and a loop on it ends. Its report is a missed check-in by the camera: it lands at the desk's next scan of that screen (witness.cameraScan, phase from the camera's id) plus witness.postCall, as a reported incident (alert.byIncident: the nth reported incident at least byIncident[n-1], and at least alert-inquiry), and the dial dispatches its response for the Alert reached to the camera's place (report.lands, alarm.dispatches); like a missed check-in it is an empty post with no body, so it holds no scene and no door. It is not gunfire: no face, no Standing, no witness. Disabling a dead camera is refused camera-dead; anyone but the Tech, only-tech; away from the cabinet, stand-at-cabinet; a camera not in the list, disable-wrong-target. Running and ordinary people (brief 054 §3.2 and §8, Sky 2026-10-25: confirmed): from people-care-alert a civilian who sees a run in their cone remembers the runner (saw-runner, a sighting with the face) and raises nothing: no found fault, no Alert; below it nobody but security minds a run. Security keep their run rule: free from Alert 2 (no clock, no memory). Nobody counts a runner while a fight is on, once a shot has been fired, or while the runner is under fire (the loud run). Engine 0.30.0 (brief 057 §2, Sky 2026-10-24: the robot follows the drawn path and moves smoothly): a Reroute's false orders still run `reroute.away` seconds from its landing, and while they run the patrol sees nothing; with `reroute.walk` it walks the walk grid at that pace from where it stood to the wait spot (patrol-reroute) and waits there facing away, and when they run out it walks back at the same pace to the point of its sweep it meets as it arrives (waiting there for the sweep if early), seeing by its facing cone as a machine does, and is back on its sweep then (patrol.sweep); a chase, an alarm or a fall ends the walk back. Without `reroute.walk` it is placed at the wait spot and back on its sweep at once.

unclaimed.rule: An unclaimed shooting is filed as a gang shooting (Motive Q1 a): when the cell shoots at the rival crew or its car and nobody of security saw it (the gunfire's reporter is 'heard', not a camera, the guard, the patrol or a unit), no city person saw the shooter or the target (witness), and nobody but the crew and its car is hit, the response comes at Alert 2 as for any shooting and its Trail and Standing are charged, but the district does not seal. The seal waits for the cell to be placed (engine 0.42.0, Motive V2): (a) any security watcher (camera, guard, patrol, officer, robot) seeing an operative with a weapon drawn or firing, at any time (carrying a body or taking someone down seen is an incident: (d)); (b) during the hold (`hold` s from the response's arrival) a response officer or robot seeing an operative within `scene` of the scene (the points the unclaimed shots were fired from and the rival car's stop where it was disabled, set burning or blew); (c) a known face in the response's sight at any time; (d) a later shooting that is not unclaimed, any new incident, or Alert 3. Then the seal runs from the later of that moment and the response's arrival, as any. A blast that hits anyone but the crew claims it at once. Any rival fight, any mission. While the gang shooting is pending and unplaced, `fired` (engine 0.43.0, Motive V3): placed, a police body or robot counts an operative a foe for having fired (ai.intent fired); unplaced, it does not (nobody of security saw who fired: a shot security saw places the cell by (a)); 'always' is 0.42.0's rule (has ever fired).

unclaimed.reason: Q1 (a): the veteran's shot at the incoming rival car can win, hard: nobody near, all four firing, then the rest of the mission at Alert 2 out of the response's sight. It matches the rule that a body moved before the police arrive leaves the report unfounded.

security.rule: Who answers gunfire and how fast. A report calls the response unit (`weapons.health.responseOfficers` officers); the earliest arrival wins and the district seals after it arrives (the seal is the security level's, `response.levels`). The delay is by who reported: a civilian witness, a guard, camera or patrol that saw it, nobody (unseen), a civilian shot. These delays are the arrivals at security level 1 (routine, today's 12 s dispatch): at another level a report lands the same seconds after the shot and the unit rolls that level's dispatch later, so the arrival moves by the dispatch's difference. A downed guard is missed at his next check-in mark (`response.checkIn`; brief 013 retires the 18 s check-in). Gunfire draws the rivals within `rivals.drawn` and the patrol within `patrol.breakTo`. A hostile who first sees the cell outside a fight reacts in `weapons.react`, then fires at its weapon's cadence (Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md: replaces aim 3 s and the per-unit fire rates). Engine 0.30.0 (`sealWarns`; Suture's bot pass, 2026-10-24: the district sealed with no warning when the response's call set the clock): every path that sets the seal clock says so in the log: a call of the response logs seal.starts with the seal's time, the unit's arrival and the report it began from; a confirmation logs seal.starts as before; the loud final fight's fight.loud states it.

sheet.rule: The stat sheet (brief 080; replaces the counted hit outside the fight lab). A shot's chance is a sum anyone can read: aim (by class, plus the character's `offset`, 0 for now) + range (point inside weapons.pointBlank, eff inside the weapon's effective ring, long to its max) + cover (the target still beside cover, in its arc, past point blank: full or partial; a running target past point blank takes targetRunning in its place) + movement (the shooter walking, running or running away, and pinned), kept between limit.min and limit.max. Each shot draws once, from the shooter's own stream (seed/id/shot, by its shot number), hit or miss; damage is the weapon's, fixed, no criticals; a read of the odds never draws. Streaks lean the player's way, and the how-to-play says so: after streak.hits in a row from one hostile on one agent, the next misses; after streak.misses in a row from one agent on one target, the next hits, if the chance is streak.floor or more. One agent takes at most one hit every `intake`, whoever is firing: focus fire lands fast, never faster, and a shot inside the gap misses (it draws all the same). A miss never hits anyone else. Enforcer at warnHealth or below: the warning, once (enforcer.warning, Game.EnforcerWarnedAt). weapons.acc and weapons.mod now serve only the fight lab and test-only pre080 runs. Guards walk and run back at guardSpeed; every other pace is unchanged.

weapons.settle: A shooter whose run ends (it stands or walks again, after a click run or a driven run that moved) waits `aimNew` before its next shot: its next shot is no sooner than aimNew after the tick the run ends. It keeps its target, its fire order and the pair's accumulator (a reset would hand back the reset-kite exploit). The same for every shooter that runs (today only the cell runs). No new value: today's aimNew, the lab's fight.lab.aimNew. Sky 2026-10-21 (the settle, a direction Sky approved; Motive briefs/027/motive/tuning.md §10.2), engine 0.16.0, both presets.
weapons.trigger: The driven agent fires with its trigger (tuning.md §11, Sky on firing 2026-10-21, brief 024): a logged input (op, on or off, target, tick). Pressed, it fires at its target on the weapon's cadence while it has reach and a line; a press fires exactly one shot at the first ready tick, a press in the cooldown is never dropped and buys that one shot only (a buffer of one, not a queue), lost if the agent aims at something else, the target goes, or it has no reach or line when the gun is ready. Released, it keeps its target and its count: a press on the same target fires on cadence with no aimNew and no reset (no tap reset). A press ends the agent's own fire order (the trigger takes over); a fire order given to it ends the trigger; control ending clears it. A lock is a lasting fire order; a locked agent is engaged, and so is an agent returning fire on its own shooter (a draw sets stance return, never at will; in the lab too since tuning.md §13.4). Follow: a cell agent that is drawn, not locked, not holding (hold fires only when ordered: a holding agent never follows and is never locked by a press, tuning.md §13.2), not returning fire, not busy, not carrying, not inside or in the car, standing within `follow` of the driven agent, with its own reach and line to the target, follows: it never walks and never draws to follow, and joins as any new target is taken (aimNew, the settle). With the follow setting off, followers fire at the target only while the trigger is held and keep their aim on release; on, a press or a change of target while pressed locks each follower at that tick (a fire order with its walk-in spent: it lapses `lineLapse` out of line and never walks). The engine derives the followers in operative id order with integer distances and logs them (fire.follow, fire.lock); the setting is the start's followLock or a logged follow order.

free.rule: Weapons free (tuning.md §14; Sky, brief 041: "Syndicate fights" adopted 2026-10-21; Sky's §14 note: a fight lasts while there is contact, not a clock). A logged cell input ({do: free, op: cell, on}, on its tick; at the start the start's weaponsFree, else `start`). While it is on and a fight is on, a drawn cell agent at stance return or free with no fire order (a lock, a focus click), no trigger and no follow picks its own target: whoever is attacking it (a combatant whose gun aims at it, or its last shooter within lineLapse), else the nearest combatant (integer distance, ties in combatant id order) within its max ring on a line; it keeps that target while it stays a combatant in reach and line, and changes only for an attacker when the one in hand is not one. It never fires on a non-combatant, never at stance hold, never draws and never walks. Precedence: a fire order (lock or focus), then the trigger, then follow, then weapons free; in a fight under weapons free follow takes only a target that is no combatant (the opening shot, a car, a camera, a calm guard); off, a drawn agent returns fire as before. Cease (X) stands an agent down: it picks again only once it is shot at after that, given a fire order or a trigger, or when the fight goes off. A fight is on from a shot by or at the cell while any combatant up and an operative up on the street are within that combatant's weapon's max ring of each other on a clear line (contact), and goes off `settle` after the last contact or shot: its length comes from damage, health and cadence. A focus (a fire order with focus: true) is a lock: lasting until its target is down, its walk-in spent. The engine derives every pick from hashed state and logs it (fire.free); the host never issues one.

oneInput.rule: One input (brief 039, Sky's call (a), 2026-10-26; GDD v0.28.0 §06 orders). F draws or holsters (draw, holster); a drawn agent fights on his own (weapons free, always on: whoever shoots at him, else the nearest combatant in reach on a line; never anyone not fighting the cell); a right hold on a hostile is a fire order, in a fight the focus (weapons.focus). In the final fight a drawn agent fights on his own from the spring (or from a loud run's start), contact or not, so the log never says the fight is off there (fire.free-off, engine 0.35.1, Motive's ruling 1), and says the fight is on (fire.free-on) once per fight: only with no fire.free-on since the last fire.free-off (engine 0.35.2, Fable briefs/039/fable-fight-on.md; log only). The cease, stance, panic and free orders are retired: each is refused unknown-verb (unknown = reject), and a start's weaponsFree is not read (weapons free is on). `on` false, or the block absent (a rulebook pinned before engine 0.35.0): the four orders are taken as before.

focus.rule: The sticky focus (brief 039; GDD v0.28.0 §06 sticky focus; revises Sky's "keep them firing until out of range", 2026-10-22). A fire order (a focus or not) ends only when its target is down, broken (a final-fight hostile breaking) or gone, on a new fire order, an act (cell.cancel's acts: any order that engages the agent), a holster, or the fight's end (fight.over). Out of reach or out of line it waits: no fire.out-of-range, no fire.lapses; the agent fights on his own meanwhile (weapons free's pick, logged fire.focus-waits once a wait), then takes the focus back once it has reach and a line (aimNew to aim, 1.0 s; the pair's count is kept). A fire order given out of range still walks in first (weapons.close). `sticky` false, or the block absent: engine 0.34's ends (out of range once reached, the line lapse).

takeCover.rule: Readable cover (brief 039; GDD v0.28.0 §06 cover). Cover within `reach` of a drawn agent in a fight is his to take: a move on the ground (a point, never a named place or a car) by a drawn, undriven agent while a fight is on (a shot by or at the cell, or the final fight) that ends within `snap` of a cover point (present, at least partial, held by nobody else, joined to the end by a straight walkable line, within `reach` of the agent) ends on that point: its kneel point, the site's point 0.85 m off the prop on the side it shields, so the prop stands between him and the shooter. Of several, the one that shields against the nearest combatant first, then the nearest, then the lower id. He holds the point while he walks to it or stands within ai.cover.snap of it; the shield itself is ai.cover's (inside the arc, still, never inside point blank). Host reads: Game.PreviewMoveSnap (the snap test, and whether the end beats the focus's cover), Game.CoverMarks, Game.PostureOf (the kneel point). Absent (a rulebook pinned before 0.35.0) the snap is the lab's only.

pin.rule: Pinned (brief 039 B, cover and pin; GDD v0.28.0 §06 pinned). Anyone shot at, hit or miss, is pinned for `s` from the tick the round lands (Gun.ShotByTick), renewed by each round; Covering fire pins everyone it covers until it ends. A pinned shooter fires at `mod` (per mille, after every other modifier). With `hold`, a pinned final-fight hostile holds: it doesn't advance (alerted, a lapsed engage, the hold's walk back to its stand or its no-stall advance wait), and a pinned body takes no kite step that closes (police closing in, a rival's walk to its ring when no cover hides it); a walk already under way goes on, and a step to cover or out of a line when shot at is still taken. `cell` (Motive sets it, GDD v0.28.0 §06): the cell's agents are pinned by hostile fire too (they fire at half; the player still commands their moves); off, only hostiles are pinned. Off from engine 0.35.1 (Motive's ruling 7, 2026-10-26, on Sky's "too punishing"; Sky can overrule it): the pin is the player's tool, and the portrait's under-fire state stays as the warning. A start's pinCell overrides it for one run. Presentation: in cover and not pinned, a person kneels; pinned in cover, he ducks behind it; pinned in the open, he cowers (Game.PostureOf, Game.PinLeft). Off (the block absent): nobody is pinned.

moves.rule: One move each (brief 039; GDD v0.28.0 §06 moves): an order with its price like any other, ready again `ready` after it is given (move-cooling, with the tick it is ready). Mark (mark, the Scout's; target a combatant she sees within mark.reach): for mark.s the marked hostile's cover doesn't count against the cell's shots (one mark at a time; a new one replaces it); Game.MarkOf reads it and his walk's end (his next move). Talk down (talk-down, the Fixer's; target a final-fight rival up, within talk.reach on a line, never police: talk-police): once talk.down of the crew are down (talk-none-down) and he is hurt (below his health, with talk.hurt: talk-not-hurt) he breaks as the crew breaks (gun down, to the crew's car), and he counts to the crew's break as one down; the blocker too: talked down he breaks and holds the car no more, so the car is free without a kill (Sky's call (c)). The Fixer shouts for talk.s, busy in the open, no firing (an act: it ends her fire order). Steam (steam, the Tech's; target a heat-main grille, the site's or a start's test grilles, within steam.reach: steam-no-grille when none is in reach, no-target for an id that is none): for steam.s no line passes within steam.r of the grille (sight, fire and every watcher's line). Covering fire (covering-fire, the Enforcer's; target a combatant within his carbine's max ring on a line; the one fire while he holds Vale, Sky's call (b)): for cover.s he fires a round every cover.every ticks at it, each a shot that never hits (shot.covering: it pins its target and costs as gunfire), and every hostile within cover.r of the target is pinned until it ends; his own fire waits meanwhile and his fire order ends (an act), he walks on. A holstered carbine draws first (the draw in its time). Out of play from engine 0.35.1 (Sky 2026-10-26, via Main: "don't think I agreed to the special moves at this stage of the dev process"): `on` false, and the block absent (a rulebook pinned before 0.35.0), refuse the four verbs unknown-verb (unknown = reject); the values and the rule stay for when Sky takes them up.

weapons.rule: Who carries what and how a shot lands (Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md; since brief 080 a shot rolls on `sheet`: the counted hit below is the fight lab's only). The Enforcer carries the carbine (the cell's); every other operative may carry a pistol, one per `sidearmArms` of Arms (the Handover issues all three); the guard, the patrol, officers and rivals carry pistols; the Enforcer, officers, the guard and the patrol are trained. A shot's accuracy is its band's (inside `pointBlank`, inside the weapon's eff, inside its max) times each modifier that applies, in per mille: the shooter's gait this tick (tuning.md §8.3, Sky 2026-10-21: a walk `mod.moving`, a run toward or across `mod.running`, a run away, its step within `runAwayCone` degrees of straight away from the target, `mod.runningAway`), the target still beside cover (`mod.cover`; with `pointBlankCover` false, never inside `pointBlank`: Sky 2026-10-21, tuning.md §8.4, as the lab) or, for a target running this tick past point blank, `mod.targetRunning` in its place (one step, never with cover), the Enforcer holding Vale (`mod.vale`), an untrained shooter (`mod.untrained`). Hits are deterministic: each shooter keeps an integer accumulator on each target, the pair's for the mission (tuning.md §13.1, engine 0.18.0, as the lab's aim memory): taking a target resumes the count the shooter left on it and nothing resets it (a switch, cease, hold, holster, a release); a target it has not fired at starts at `acc.start`; each shot adds the accuracy, and at 1000 or more the shot hits and 1000 comes off (750: exactly three in four). A shot does the weapon's damage; health per kind is `health`, at 0 down. The cost moves from the shot to the victim: +`costs.gunfire` T once per shooting (the first shot at each target, hit or miss), +`costs.hit` T per person hit, once, and +`costs.down` more when they go down; the final fight stays untraced (fight.traced). A drawn weapon seen by security raises Alert to `costs.drawSeenSecurity` and that watcher engages; seen by people, it is one witnessed incident (Alert at least `costs.drawSeenPeople`, standing per traceable weapon-drawn), and drawings within `costs.drawWindow` and witness range of it are the same incident (Motive addendum 2026-10-15). Fire on the move (tuning.md §8.2): a fire order stops a walker (it stands and fires, or walks in when out of reach or line) and never stops a runner (the run goes on, firing at its gait; out of reach it walks in once the run ends); a driven agent keeps its drive and fires at each tick's gait; a move given while a fire order stands keeps the order and fires on the move, and spends its walk-in (out of reach when the move ends, it holds its aim `lineLapse` and lapses; a new fire order walks in again); stances fire at the gait's chance. Engine 0.21.0 (Sky 2026-10-22, brief 041: "Keep them firing until out of range I would say, same for running"): a lasting fire order (the fire order, a lock, a focus) that has had its target in reach (the weapon's max ring) and line on some tick ends at once when the target is beyond that ring, whether the agent walks, runs, is driven or stands, or the target moves (log fire.out-of-range; no walk back in, no lapse); a new act (an order that engages the agent: watch, listen, turn, call, loop, reroute, mislead, takedown, carry, drop, stash, restrain, enter, take, board) ends it (log fire.cancelled); until it has had reach and line, the walk-in and the lapse above stand. Anyone can be shot (tuning.md §9, Sky 2026-10-21) but the cell's own agents. Orders: draw (`draw` ticks), holster (`holster`), stance (hold, return, free), fire until down (first shot `aimNew` after taking the target; holds aim `lineLapse` when the line breaks), cease, panic (once a fight is on). A civilian or a contact is a target only when the order says so (the host's right hold and the ring's Fire always say so, brief 041: the hold is the confirmation). Tuning.md §9 (engine 0.15.0): Vale, a final-fight hostile after fight.over, a knocked-out or restrained person where they lie (a hit kills them: a takedown kill's consequences plus the gunfire's), a response unit or robot by its own id and a camera ("camera:<id>", `health.camera`; shot out it is dark for the mission; gunfire only: no hit or down Trail, no Standing) are all targets; a person shot down outside the final fight lies dead where they fell (a brief-013 body); the cell's own agents are the one target refusal (fire-on-cell). An order whose shot would fail the mission (Vale; the driver while Vale is out) always takes the `costs.loudHold` hold. Brief 030 (Sky 2026-10-20): `close`: a fire order on a target out of the weapon's reach, or with no clear line, walks the grid (at a walk) to the nearest free point inside its effective reach with a clear line (within 60 m of walk; none: refused out-of-range or no-clear-line), stands there and fires; it holds while it walks (no lapse), and a driven agent is not walked (the host drives; the order holds). `autoHolster`: a weapon drawn by a fire order or by panic (not by a draw order) is holstered by the engine `autoHolster` seconds after the fight it was drawn for ends (fight.public: quiet after its last shot, the final fight at fight.over), unless the agent still has a fire order, a stance order was given since the draw, or a hostile combatant up within its weapon's max reach has a clear line to the agent (then at the first tick none has); a weapon drawn with a draw order stays drawn until holstered.
weapons.reason: Sky approved Motive's five answers on 2026-10-15; the numbers are Motive's calculator's (briefs/011/motive-fights/fights.py), [S] until Suture's frontier runs on the engine.

ai.noStall: The safe fight can't stall (engine 0.34.0; Motive briefs/067/motive-square.md, motive-values.json M067-SQ2; Pulse's motion): in the final fight a rival holding (hold) with no foe in his effective reach for `engageLapse` advances again, as from engage, on the nearest operative standing on the street that he has cause to fire on (ai.intent; the Vale holder counts): to the cover that shields him from that operative (ai.seek.rival) and closes on him (engine 0.34.1, Aster's ruling within SQ2: of the points the cover rule gives, in its order, the first whose walk to him is strictly shorter than the walk from where the rival stands, and which lies inside the rival's effective reach of him or nearer him than he stands), else to his stop point of that operative: the first point of the walk to him within `stopReach` of his effective reach from which he sees him (a rival inside that ring with a wall between them walks on until he has the line), not of the car's point. On the advance (to the cover or the stop point) he takes no kite step out of a line, as on the walk to a held car (fight.unguarded): he walks on until a foe is in his reach (then stops and engages, as any advance) or he is there. With the cover rule alone a kite step turned each walk back to the cover he had left (ra-h3, every 2.2-2.5 s). With nowhere to go that closes he holds and looks again `engageLapse` later, saying nothing. No new value. Police and the blocker hold their posts as built. Why: a rival in hold never advanced again, and an advance without cover stopped at stopReach of 15 m from the car's point while the cell stood round the car, so on the square without its planters the last rivals held 15 m out with 2 of 5 down: the crew never broke and fight.over never came (logged ai.advance). And (0.34.1) an advance that only left out the cover he held let a rival between two covers go back and forth every 1.8 s, never nearer anyone (ra-h3: rival-3, cv-030 and cv-029, 4:13.9-4:21.1).

intent.rule: Who a hostile fires on before the final fight, per agent (Sky 2026-10-21: "each character has their own history, scout for example is stealth - shouldn't be punished if enforcer goes in wild"): an agent is a foe for what that agent is seen doing or for its own known face, never for another agent's acts; a foe is shot only inside the body's effective reach (its max ring when shot at, tuning.md §7.10) on its own line. Kinds: rivals (the crew and the ambush), robots (the patrol, the response's robots), police (everyone else armed: the guard, the response unit, police units, officers). Foes: drawn (a weapon out, in its sight), fired (has fired; while a gang shooting is pending and unplaced, only once the cell is placed: security.unclaimed.fired, engine 0.43.0, Motive V3), vale (holds Vale), violence (security saw it do violence), face (security knows its face: it saw it draw, saw it do violence or gave it a warning, or a witness's report landed that remembers it doing violence or drawing; loitering is a found fault, never a face), seen (the rival crew saw it with a weapon out, firing, in a takedown or a carry). Police: `foes` always, face from `face`; a drawn weapon they see at Alert up to warn.maxAlert, before any shot, on an agent with no target (no fire order, lock, focus or trigger: one about to fire gets no beat), gets the drop-it warning (warn.ticks, at most warn.perWatcher a watcher; Alert to warn.alert; heeded: +warn.trail and the face is known; held: drawn-seen) and is no foe while it runs; from `closeIn`, at security level closeLevel and up, a police body (the response unit before it joins, a police unit at its scene) that sees a foe beyond its effective ring closes in on the sighting by fight.kite's close-in; an Alert alone never makes anyone a foe. Robots: `foes`, face from `face`, or at any Alert while the cell's Heat band is in `faceHeat` (Pulse §2.3, Sky's answer 4); no warning, no close-in. Rivals: they watch the street from their arrival (their cone, rulebook perception.rivals); calm, `calm`; alerted (drawn by gunfire, or from alertedAt), `alerted`, and the drawn crew presses for the Vale holder (its stop point of him, re-planned each fight.kite.replan) while he holds Vale on the street. A guard or patrol not yet engaged engages an agent that is a foe by face when it sees him. A fight the rivals start costs the cell no Standing (fight.public: fired first is the cell's only). In the final fight (`final`): agent (PROVISIONAL, tuning.md §15.2; Sky 2026-10-22 "I think so - sounds right", to confirm after playing it), a hostile fires on an operative only for that operative's own causes, the same lists as before the fight (police and robots: drawn, fired, vale, violence, or its own known face, the final fight being at Alert 2 or more; rivals: drawn, vale, seen), so an agent kept out of it stays out of it; every, every operative is a foe (the rule before engine 0.20.0, Pulse §2.1). The fight range is always every (it has no history to read). The rival crew's guard ally is a foe in the final fight either way. Nobody draws for the cell: an agent fired on is shown under fire (the host's UnderFireOf), never drawn by it (Sky's answer 1).
