ai.rule: What a hostile does in a fight (Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §2–3; Sky approved real-time shoot-outs, briefs/011/motive-fights.md). One machine: routine, alerted (react; summoned bodies skip it; an ambush waits weapons.aimNew, plus fight.safe.warn if Inez warned), advance (to the cover point the site's cover data gives, else to stopReach of its weapon's effective reach short of its foe or objective; fires as it moves, at weapons.mod for its gait: tuning.md §8.3, Sky 2026-10-21, both presets), engage (a foe inside its effective reach on a clear line: stops, takes its target by class: 1 whoever fired at it within weapons.lineLapse (for a police body, any operative who did, not only the last: tuning.md §12.2; the target it aims at stays while its shooter keeps firing), 2 the operative holding Vale, 3 the nearest with a weapon drawn, 4 the nearest; keeps it until down, out of reach or sight for lineLapse, or a better class appears; a new target costs aimNew; steps to cover when unprotected, once each cover.stepGap, and leaves a point unprotected for cover.leave; cover.stepFires (true): that step fires at the walk's chance; false is tuning.md §8.3's fallback, measured and not adopted: a rival walking to the cover it stepped to, and an operative on a cover-snap walk, fire nothing; advances, closes and lanes still fire), hold (holders: police, the patrol, a guard; a target reacquired within reacquire is shot at once), break (rivals: more than half the crew down; they run for their car and are gone within rivalGone; no longer combatants, no longer hold the car, no Trail), down. Lapse to hold or advance after engageLapse with no foe in reach. A body beside a cover point (cover.snap) that shields it, standing still, past point blank, is hit at weapons.mod.cover (quality ≥ qFull) or modPartial (≥ qPartial). One body to a cover point. Seek: how far each looks for cover. Police (officers) hold their stand and never break; the response unit joins the loud fight at the nearest police stand (overflow beside a taken one, else the nearest free cover within seek.police); the guard ally runs to his post, taking cover within seek.ally; an engaging guard fights from where he stands and stands down guardReturn after his last foe; the patrol chases to the shot's origin and resumes its sweep patrolResume after its last foe. Shots resolve together at the end of a tick. The crowd's scatter (Pulse §4) is not in yet.
ai.src: Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md (brief 011); Sky 2026-10-15 approved Motive's briefs/011/motive-fights.md
ai.reason: Pulse's spec, every number his proposal and Motive's to tune; the crowd's values wait for the crowd's states.

crowd.rule: The crowd in a fight (Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4). A person of the city's people on the street is startled by a shot whose shooter stands within `scatter`, seen or not, or by an operative's drawn weapon within witness range on a clear line: they stand `startle` ticks (a Fearful person `startleFearful`), then flee at `run` by the grid to a refuge of the site's cover data (a door or a street mouth) within `fleeMax` that ends farther from the shooter than they stand, the nearest (ties on id), or if none the refuge farthest from the shooter; there they are sheltered, off the street. `quiet` after the last shot they walk back at `walk` to the stop their routine has for the clock. `walk` is the city's walking pace (engine 0.34.0, Motive M067-B1): everyone the engine walks itself walks at it (the summoned partner, a reporter or teller to a phone, a witness to a body, the crowd back from shelter), and the rounds bake is checked against it; the cell walks at cell.speed. Witnesses are taken at the shot, before any startle: a person within witness range with a clear line to the shooter or the target remembers saw-gunfire (place, time, the face). Nobody is hit by a stray shot. A person on the street who is not sheltered blocks a watcher's sightline (the guard, the patrol, a camera, the response unit) that passes within `occlude` of them, between two bodies' width of either end; a hostile's own aim ignores people. The four people the Handover casts by role keep their roles: they do not scatter.
crowd.src: Pulse, briefs/011/pulse-fight-ai.md §4; §06 citizen actions; §05 crowds block guard and camera sightlines
crowd.reason: Pulse's spec; the cast by role keep their places so the mission's contacts stay where its rules need them (Keel).

summon.rule: The summons (Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md §1.3): a turned contact who is called sends for their lover (people.rules ties.kinds.lover), read from the city's ties, never from the mission. The lover leaves where he is, walks the grid to the caller at the city's walking pace (crowd.walk; cell.speed until engine 0.34.0), stays `stay` and walks back. A caller who remembers `pressed.act` (any of it: helped then pressured counts) warns him when he reaches her: he stays `pressed.stay` and runs back at `pressed.speed`, so the door is clear for less; nothing else changes (brief 085, Sky). Refused, at no cost and with its code, when he is off the street, busy (down, held, engaged in a fight, or already away), more than `walkMax` away, Alert is above `alertMax`, he holds a memory of the cell's gunfire, violence or drawn weapon, or he has come `perShift` times this shift. Alert reaching above `alertMax` ends the visit: he heads straight back at a guard's pace (weapons.sheet.guardSpeed), unless he is already on a pressed run back, which goes on at `pressed.speed`. The visit is no act of the cell: the call keeps cell.call.trail. A contact's role job (the driver's camera block) is the call's other use.
summon.src: Motive, briefs/011/motive-lovers.md (2026-10-15); Sky via Aster: Inez and the door guard are lovers, and her call pulls him off the door
summon.reason: systems over scripts: any turned contact with an eligible lover is a lure, in every generated mission (Motive §1.3). Keel models the visit for a lover with a post (the guard), as the Handover needs; another lover is refused until a routine can be left.

cancel.rule: A cancel order stops what one operative is doing now, the activity the HUD shows: an act in progress first, then a walk or run, then a fire order, then a draw, then a downed operative carried. Each verb's line says what cancelling it costs or keeps. stop: the operative stands where they are. holster: a draw not yet done goes back. cease: the fire order ends, the weapon stays drawn. lost: the act's time is spent and nothing lands (Watch and Listen learn nothing; a Loop, Reroute, Mislead or lift not finished does nothing; their Trail is charged only when they land). aborted: the approach stops mid-conversation; the money held for it comes back (the engine holds the price at the order and pays it only in the outcome's charge, Redline E2), no Trail, and the person remembers an aborted approach (memory act `aborted`, with the Fixer's face): it is no refusal, so the approach may be tried again, but it is a fact an investigator can get. A loop that has landed runs on its own (cell.loop.run) and is no activity of the Tech's, so there is nothing to cancel (cancel.loopHeld retired with the tether, engine 0.31.0). staff-report: the Enforcer comes back out without Vale by the public door, or by the service door if a unit holds the public door, or waits inside while both are held (response; brief 013 E3); the Office staff report the intruder, one reported incident (alert.byIncident). vale-reports: Vale is let go at his car and reports the attempt, one reported incident, and he remembers the aborted take (memory act `aborted`, the Enforcer's face), so an investigator who questions him finds a lead (Motive addendum Q4). put-down: the carried operative is laid down where the carrier stands. Go is instant and has nothing to cancel; a Board or a step-out cancelled spends the time and lands nothing (lost). Putting Vale down is no cancel: the Enforcer keeps him (a rule of its own if Sky wants one). The verbs whose line may change take one of: turn aborted or lost; enter staff-report or quiet; take vale-reports or quiet. Brief 013: a takedown cancelled before it lands lets the victim go (`takedown` released): he saw the Enforcer and reports it as a woken victim would; lifting, dropping, stashing or tying a body cancelled spends the time and lands nothing (`body` lost); a body carried is laid down where the carrier stands (`carrying` put-down). A Drive under way is no cancel (`driveCar` drives-on; engine 0.33.1, Fable's question): the getaway car stops only at a stand (cell.driveCar), so it drives on to the one it was given and everyone in it rides on; the cancel is refused car-driving, for the driver and the riders alike.
cancel.src: Sky 2026-10-15 playtest: "there's nothing showing me what the cell player is doing when they're busy, nor is there a way to cancel their action" (Aster)
cancel.reason: Accepted by Motive (addendum 2026-10-15 Q4; no put-Vale-down rule in the Handover). Keel's proposal: cancelling an act already under way spends its time and lands nothing, as a refusal does; the money held comes back because it was never handed over; the two acts that put a stranger in front of someone (Enter, Take) leave a report, as an interrupted intrusion would; a broken-off approach leaves the person the Fixer's face but no refusal, so cancel is no free retry of a bad card but no punishment like a refusal either.

perception.rule: Mount (brief 055 §7, Motive 2026-10-24; engine 0.28.0): every watcher sees from its own eye above its own floor (the site's grid.floor, block z): a person (the guard, staff, passers-by, police, rivals, the cell) `mount.person` (eye-cm), so the guard on the Office landing sees from 75 + 160; a camera from its lens by its kind (`mount.cameras`; a camera kind not listed is rejected at the start), never blocked by its own piece; the patrol robot `mount.patrol`; the response's robots `mount.robot`. A target is seen when the 3D line from that eye to its head (its floor + eye) or its chest (its floor + `mount.chest`) is clear: either is enough. An occluder (z, h, footprint) blocks a line that passes through the prism z..z+h over its footprint, a line touching its outline at a height it spans included. A person on the street blocks a line that passes within crowd-occlude-cm of them in plan only where the line runs below their head top (their floor + `mount.headTop`). Fire lines are sight lines (the shooter's eye to the target's head or chest). A body lying on the ground is seen as a standing person (head and chest). A watcher sees a point inside its cone (ahead within reach, and to the side within half × ahead ÷ reach), along a sightline no occluder crosses at eye height (§05 levels: 3D). A person (a walking guard, the response's officers, the rivals) also sees anyone within `near` whatever their facing; a machine (a camera, the patrol, sweeping or chasing, the response's robots) sees by its cone only (brief 031 L2, Sky 2026-10-20: "robots look futuristic, mindset is still quite old school, forward facing cameras not 360"). The guard posted at his door has no near sense for detection (his door cone only); the attention clock gives him one (attention.near). A camera's cone is its site's; a guard at his door, a walking guard, a chasing patrol, the response unit and the rivals use these. The sweeping patrol's cone widens with depth. People (brief 054 §3.3; engine 0.28.0): with `people.sees` cone a civilian sees within `people.reach` and ±60° of their facing (`people.half` at the reach), with no near sense, on a clear line; what they notice there, and when, is witness.notice; security keep the all-round sense; with `around` (or no `people`) everyone on the street sees all round as before.
perception.src: §05 cameras, watchers, levels; the top-down test's cones

sight.rule: What the cell knows of each watcher's sight (Sky 2026-10-16: cones are the Scout's skill; brief 031, Sky 2026-10-20: every agent watches). A watcher's sight is its perception cone clipped by what blocks sight; the cell knows it only once learned, and learned knowledge stays with the cell (a downed Scout keeps it). learn watch: a completed Watch (cell.watch, watch.s, $0, 0 T, no Alert of its own) of the watcher by any operative in its kind's `by` (all four) teaches its sight. The reach is the agent's, watch.reach by operative, one ring for people and machines alike, on a clear line at eye height (walls, solids and people on the street block it); every watcher teaches the same facts. The guard is watched as the person he is (cell.watch: routine), and that Watch teaches his sight too. Listen and Mislead stay the Scout's. What anyone learns is the cell's. learn arrival: the response unit and drawn rivals come for the cell, and their sight is known from the moment they are on the street. Knowledge is witnessed (watched) or told (the start state: the briefing, a previous mission). routine fixed: a camera does not move, so its routine is known with its sight; person: the guard's routine is his person routine (cell.watch); watched: the patrol's routine (when its sweep turns and when it sees the door) is known once the union of the cell's completed Watches of it, in mission time, reaches watch.routine seconds (two agents watching at once count once); none: no routine. Knowledge changes only what the cards show, never an outcome: a quote's 'seen by' shows each known watcher's true answer, and `unknown` for a watcher the cell doesn't know that stands within its kind's farthest sight of the act or route on a clear line (its facing is what the cell doesn't know), as the action card shows '?' until the temperament is known (§04, Sky Q3). Detection needs no knowledge: a watcher that sees an operative now has noticed them, known or not.
sight.src: Sky 2026-10-16 (Aster): view cones are the Scout's skill; Sky 2026-10-18 (Aster): "tech should be able to watch camera / robots like scout can"; brief 031 (Sky 2026-10-20): "all characters should be able to watch", reach per agent (Motive, briefs/031-everyone-watches.md §1) (the machines' `by`; people stay the Scout's); Glyph, briefs/011/ui/review-2026-10-16 §3.4; §03 Scout: Watch; §04 preview '?' (Sky Q3); §05 cameras, watchers
sight.reason: the GDD has every cone always on (§05 cameras: fixed visible cones). Sky approved the Scout's skill on 2026-10-16; the reach, the routine's time and the known-on-arrival rule are Keel's starting values, for Motive to price and Sky's GDD edit.

mood.rule: A person's mood toward the cell (brief 054 §4, Motive rev 4; Sky 2026-10-23: mood from any cause, the person's own life included), the first row that holds: scared (fear at least `scared.fear`, or remembers one of `scared.acts`: attacked, a takedown, gunfire or violence seen), uneasy (fear at least `uneasy.fear`: the Fearful temperament's own fear 1 reads uneasy; resentment at least `uneasy.resentment`; or remembers one of `uneasy.acts`: a threat, a drawn weapon, a carry, a found body, an alarm, anything told; or, for a security watcher, wary of an operative), friendly (loyalty at least `friendly.loyalty`, or remembers being helped or paid), else neutral. A refusal and district Standing stay out (each has its own price). The mood moves an approach's fit by `shift` (one step at most, never off the ladder): refused stays refused, worse is the floor, a step up from suits is ready (lines `ready` on turn.help, turn.pay, turn.pressure); Ask never moves. Offers (`offers`, brief 054 §2): a Watch on a person is offered only when it would teach something the cell reads: their mood (simulated, on the street, not down, not turned, the temperament not known, the mood not neutral and not the one the cell last saw), or, for security (the door guard, a job in witness.staff), their sight and marks until watched; a Watch never teaches a secret (brief 054 §9.2: only Listen does); anything else is refused nothing-to-see, free, and the host draws no row. A completed Watch stores the mood seen at its end (known, hashed when set). Listen and the approaches that require the routine need a Watch only while one is offered for that person: a person already watched never re-locks. The card: before a Watch as before; after it the known mood steps the fit of each temperament it shows (the approach it favours reads likely, Quote.Likely; the one it hurts, Quote.Hurt); once the temperament is known the card reads the true mood, exact.
mood.reason: a Watch shows one thing the cell can act on, or isn't offered (Sky 2026-10-23: "If a person being watched has no impact then we just drop that watched action")

parked.rule: The parked car noticed (engine 0.40.0). A car of the cell's standing on private ground is a loiterer: a drive (site ground.drives[]), or a bay whose use is official or service (site ground.bays[].use, Vantage's; `ground`); a public bay or the carriageway is no private ground and keeps no clock. Whether a stand is private is read at site load from where its car stands; a bay with no use rejects the site. Every watcher that keeps attention clocks (attention: the live cameras, the door guard unless he is the cell's ally, the patrol robot, the response's officers and robots) keeps one clock for the car, whether anyone is aboard or not: it sees the car in its cone, and a person also within attention.near whatever his facing, on a clear line from its eye to `sight` over the car's centre, no crowd across it. The clock is attention's: +1 s a second standing there in its sight, -1 s a second out of its sight, driving or off private ground, to 0, or to the wary mark once wary; the marks are the Heat band's (noticed, wary, report); the report is once per car per watcher per mission, lands as attention's do (a camera's at its desk's next scan plus report.call, a person's or a robot's by radio after report.call; one downed first drops his) and is a found fault: an incident (Alert to at least alert.byIncident[n-1] and at least attention.alert), no Trail, a lead (the cell's car, the place, the time), the dial's dispatch to the car. Operatives aboard keep no clocks of their own (attention: in the car is off the street); out beside it, theirs run as before. Logged car.noticed, car.wary, car.reported (made) and car.report-lands (landed). The Drive card says it (Game.ParkedQuote): who would see the car at that stand ("?" for a watcher the cell has not watched), the marks, and the patrol's return when it is rerouted.
parked.src: Motive, briefs/096/motive/rules.html and values.json (brief 096); Sky 2026-11-04: "all. recommended"; engine 0.40.0 (Keel)
parked.reason: cars stand at the kerb; a strange car on an office's drive looks wrong. One clock and one rule, already learned on people; 45 s at Heat 0 is the 30-45 s of work Sky asked for: a timed Reroute and the Tech's walk

run.rule: A run is seen and suspicious, never an Alert on its own (engine 0.34.0; brief 067, Sky playing 0.2.122: "Running shouldn't be that badly punished"; Motive M067-B2: cell.runAlert is retired). A watcher that keeps a clock, with a running operative in its sight for the clock (its live sight, and for a person attention.near), lifts its clock on him to the band's notice mark on the run's first tick in its sight (`at` notice: its cue shows noticed then) and counts each tick of the run in its sight as standing still (`counts` still: +1 s a second); out of its sight, or walking, the clock drains as for a loiterer. The stages, the wary mark and the report are attention's own: a run held in sight makes the watcher wary after (wary - notice) s and reports it after (report - notice) s (Heat 0: 12 s and 37 s), and the report lands as a loiterer's (a found fault, Alert to at least `alert`, no Trail, a sighting, the dial's response). A loud run (a fight on, a shot fired, the runner under fire) or a run at Alert 2 and above (cell.run's free cases) moves no clock. Security staff who keep no clock (a guard on the street, a witness.staff job) and anyone in witness range who would remember a run still remember it (memory saw-runner: no Trail, no Alert, no Standing); the first security watcher or security-staff person to see a run logs the sighting once a run (run.seen); a guard who saw a runner no longer fights at the cell's side. From people-care-alert a civilian who sees a run in their cone remembers the face (Sky's 054 call, kept).
run.src: Sky playing 0.2.122 (brief 067 item 6; routing B: "running seen and suspicious but not an Alert on its own"); Motive briefs/067/motive.md §1.3, motive-values.json M067-B2
run.reason: readable: the first tick a watcher sees a run its cue shows noticed, so the player learns that running is seen without an Alert to learn it from; proportional: one pass costs the cue, a run held in sight costs as loitering does, and more with Heat. Motive's probe (briefs/067/motive/results/run-camera.txt): the Scout running 16 legs across the entrance camera is noticed at 0:16.3, wary 0:28.2, reported 0:53.2, landed 0:57.6 (Alert 1); route A ends at Alert 0 (0.33.1: 1); no quiet reference route gains a report

attention.rule: Watchers notice loiterers (brief 031 §2; Sky 2026-10-20: "standing in an observed area for a while without moving causes alert. So standing behind a camera's LoS is fine"). Every security watcher on the street keeps one clock per operative: each live camera (not looped, not blocked), the door guard (not the cell's ally), the patrol robot and the response's officers and robots; civilians and rivals keep none. Each tick, for each operative on the street (not inside, not in the car, not down or carried): in the watcher's sight and standing still, idle or Watching, the clock runs +1 s a second; in sight in any other act (Listen, a turn, Call, Loop, Reroute, Mislead, Enter, Take, a takedown, carrying a body or Vale, restraining, stashing: Sky L1) it holds; moving, or out of its sight, it drains 1 s a second, to 0, or to the wary mark once wary. In sight (`sense`): a machine (cone) by its perception cone only; a person (near) by his cone and anyone within `near` on a clear line whatever his facing, the guard posted at his door included (for the clock only: a takedown's awareness at the order keeps his cone). People on the street block sight. The marks are the band's (by the cell's Heat, read once at the mission's start from the start state's `heat`, else the mission's start.heat, else 0; the band is the last whose heatFrom the Heat reaches): at `notice` the watcher has noticed the operative (a warning only); at `wary` it is wary of him for the rest of the mission (its clock never drains below the wary mark again; a wary person is aware of him at a takedown: unarmed he struggles, the armed guard draws); at `report` it reports a loiterer, once per operative per watcher per mission: a camera's report lands at its watcher's next scan (`report.scan`, phase from the camera's id, as witness.cameraScan) plus `report.call`; a person's or a robot's by radio after `report.call`; a person or robot downed before it lands drops it. A loiterer reported is a found fault: Alert to at least `alert`, no Trail, logged as a sighting (watcher, operative, place, time), and the dial dispatches its response for the Alert reached (an alarm with no body: counts topped up, never repeated). A run in its sight counts too (attention.run, engine 0.34.0). Heat = campaign Trail + Menace (max(0, −Standing)), fixed for the mission (§05).
attention.src: brief 031 §2 (approved by Sky 2026-10-20: D1, D3, L1, L2, L3); Motive, briefs/031-everyone-watches.md; probe briefs/031/loiter-probe-heat0.txt
attention.reason: generous at the start (the Handover is Heat 0: a 20 s Watch from inside a sight line just reaches wary, only a 45 s stand reports); wary within a Watch's 20 s in every band, so a whole Watch in sight always makes the watcher wary (D1); only when infamous is the report (18 s) shorter than a Watch. Tuned by play.

takedown.rule: The Enforcer's takedown (brief 013, Sky 2026-10-16: anyone can be targeted; one rule set for every simulated person, no named target list). The Enforcer alone, standing within `reach` of a person on the street, knocks them out (`ko`) or kills them (`kill`); silent: none of the gunfire rules apply, no money. Vale may be killed (the mission fails, §07) but not knocked out (use Take); the patrol and cameras are no targets (Reroute and Loop are their verbs). A target who had the Enforcer in his cone when the order was given, heard him running within witness range, or witnessed one of the cell's acts this mission (a takedown, a carry, a drawn weapon: Motive rev 3, until a stop has a facing) is aware: unarmed, he struggles (`struggle` more), screams (heard within witness.scream) and holds the Enforcer's face; armed (a person with a weapon: the door guard), the takedown fails, he draws and engages (Alert at least weapons.costs.drawSeenSecurity at sight). The victim lies where he fell until moved: a body. A knocked-out victim wakes after `wake`, staggers `stagger`, then reports the assault whatever his temperament (a cell contact says nothing); a dead one never wakes or talks. Any operative carries a body (cell.carry lift, then walk only: the Enforcer at cell.speed, the others at carry.untrained; no run, no fire) and puts it down in carry.drop; restrains a living one in `restrain` (no move, no call-out, still seen on open ground; a finder frees him in `free`, then he reports); stashes it, standing at the stash, into a container (`stash.container`, on the street, seen as a carry) or through a service door (`stash.door`, off-screen; a door holds `stash.doorHolds` bodies, a storeroom: rev 4 R4.3; a container what its site entry says). Only a stash hides a body (two hide levels, open and shut; Sky merged call 6). A woken, unrestrained victim in a stash calls out every `callOut`, heard within witness.scream. A container is emptied by a round every `service.period`, its phase from its id, standing `service.dwell`: a body inside is found then (in the mission only; Sky merged call 9). Every number of the takedown, the price and its forecast are on the order's card before it is given.

notice.rule: Who notices what, by act and Alert (brief 054 §3.2, Motive rev 4; Sky 2026-10-24: "Ordinary people shouldn't really care unless there's high alert status - think real world. And yeah, would be in cone area only for seeing"). Read only when perception.people.sees is cone. A civilian (anyone on the street not security: security is the door guard and a job in `staff`) sees a point within perception.people.reach in their cone (perception.people.half at the reach) on a clear line, and a body within 1.5 m is found whatever the facing (`near`: an act in `near.acts` within `near.cm` on a clear line, any facing, at every Alert; every act in `near.acts` is an `always` act; brief 054 §9.1, Motive: a takedown, the Take's struggle and a carry stay cone-only, a stashed body is not open): `always` at every Alert (violence: a drawn weapon, a takedown and the Take's struggle, carrying a body or Vale, an open body); `odd` only from Alert `from` (Pressure, a running face, Vale's escort grip: below it ordinary people mind their own business); `never` at any Alert (the private approaches, and acts only security or machines read). `heard` turns heads: gunfire, a person shot and a car blown are seen all round within witness-range-m on a clear line, any facing; a hearer of a scream within witness-range-m on a clear line turns and sees what is there. Security see as before at every Alert: all round within witness-range-m on a clear line, plus their cones. Once noticed, the reaction is witness.rule's list, unchanged. Every act a witness path asks about is in exactly one list; unknown = reject. Sky confirmed both refining rows on 2026-10-25 (brief 054 §8: "Your recommendation seem good"): `threat` is `odd` (Pressure is unseen by ordinary people below Alert `from`, seen from it; security see it at every Alert) and `run` is `odd` (from Alert `from` a civilian who sees a run in their cone remembers the runner, saw-runner, a sighting with the face, and raises nothing: no found fault, no Alert; nobody counts a runner during a loud run: a fight on, a shot fired, the runner under fire).

witness.rule: What a person does when the city's silent violence reaches them (Pulse's decision list; Motive's numbers). Who notices: a takedown or a carry, everyone on the street within witness range on a clear line at any tick of it; an open body, the same, checked every `check.ticks` (phase from the body's id); a live camera, the guard, the patrol and the response's units in their cones; a shut body nobody. The rows, first that holds, evaluated when the person notices: staff (a job in `staff`, or the door guard): radio from where he stands, landing react + postCall (the armed guard, the patrol and the response's units seeing an act or a carry engage instead: Alert at least weapons.costs.drawSeenSecurity at sight); kin of the victim (a tie in `kin`): report at once, whatever the temperament (fear `terrifiedFear`: flee); cell (turned, or loyalty at least values.word-quiet-loyalty): quiet; an Informer (resentment at its max): report; terrified (fear at least `terrifiedFear`): flee, never report; then by temperament: Loyal reports; Idealist reports, after walking to a body to learn its state (`check`); Mercenary reports only once Alert is at least `mercenaryAlert`; Fearful flees an act or carry and avoids a body. A reporter walks the grid to the nearest report point (a staffed door: the site's door refuges; a call box), at the city's walking pace (crowd.walk) for a body and running pace (crowd.run) for an act or a carry, and calls (`call`): the report lands at the desk; a live camera's lands at its next scan (`cameraScan`, phase from its id) + postCall; a robot's after `robot`. At most `cap` reporters of one incident are in transit; one taken down, killed or carried before his report lands drops it. Whoever quiets, avoids or flees, and every reporter, tells one tie (first kind in `tells`): a tie on the street within `tell` face to face at once; a tie indoors at a unit only from a phone (calls are voice, no networks: GDD §01; Aster 2026-10-16, brief 013 E1). A reporter who walked to a report point tells from its phone when the report lands; one who radios tells face to face only, unless he stands at a report point. A quiet or avoiding person with no tie in speaking range and a tie indoors walks to the nearest report point and calls (`call`), the same walk as a report and stopped the same way (taken down, or Vale taken, before the call: nobody is told); a fleeing one calls only if the refuge her flight ends at is a staffed door. A tell is no report: it is outside `cap` and raises no Alert. A told entry, facts only, one hop (a told person never tells it on); a told Loyal person reports it from where they are. Alert rises when a report lands, never at sight (Sky merged call 1), to `alert` by what it says: a takedown seen `seen`, a carry seen `carry`, a person lying (or a noise from a stash) `down`, a dead body (staff know, an Idealist checks) `dead`, a woken victim `woken`, a missed check-in `mark`, a missing expected person `missing`; a knockout never above takedown.koAlertMax by itself; one takedown is one incident (Alert to the highest of its landed and confirmed reports; the nth reported incident at least alert.byIncident[n-1]). Witness Trail (+values.witness-trail) and Standing (traceable takedown) move once per incident at sight; a turned witness (loyalty at least values.word-quiet-loyalty) adds no Trail, and Standing still moves (Sky merged call 5). A screaming witness (fear at least `screamFear`), kin and an aware victim are heard within `scream` with no line: hearers with a line within witness range become witnesses; the rest hold heard-alarm. A reporter volunteers place and time when questioned (investigator.question, outcome volunteers). Rev 4 (Motive R4.2; Sky 2026-10-16): before every row, an accomplice of the act (a person turned to enable this very act: for the Take and its escort, the turned driver) is never its witness, whatever the tie; `kin` is lover or family only (workmate is not kin; `close`, lover, family and workmate, is whose absence or loss a person feels: expectations, the alarm's places, grief and worry). The Take: at Vale's own car with its driver turned it happens inside the car, off-screen, with no witness window (and nothing for the pickup camera to see); any other Take reads as an act for its first cell.take.struggle s, seen as a takedown by everyone within witness range on a clear line and every watcher that sees him (a live pickup camera still fails it at the order, §07). Escorted on foot, Vale looks wrong only to his kin within witness range on a clear line, or to anyone within values.near-m on a clear line who sees the grip: a carry seen. The Take and its escort are one incident, opened at the first sighting (an unseen Take opens none); witness Trail and Standing move at sight; no assault Trail is charged (the Take keeps cell.take.trailUnturned); Vale let go by a cancel reports on the same incident if it was seen. Who notices (engine 0.28.0): where this rule says everyone on the street within witness range on a clear line, it reads witness.notice (a civilian by their cone and the act x Alert rows; security all round; a scream within witness range on a clear line turns heads and its hearers notice what is there).

response.rule: The response is a dial (Sky 2026-10-16: 'it's easy to swarm the play area with robots'; merged call 3): `levels` indexed by the security level S = the district's base + its open cases (campaign) + the mission's bonus, from the mission's data; the Handover's is 2. A landed alarm (a report of a silent act, a missed check-in, a missing person; gunfire, whose report lands its security.response delay less level 1's dispatch after the shot) puts the response on the street the level's `dispatch` later: at Alert 1 `a1Robots` robots; at Alert 2 or more `a2Units` units of weapons.health.responseOfficers officers (the response unit first) and `a2Robots` robots, then one more unit every `reinforce` up to `unitCap`; Alert 3 adds `a3Units` units to the district mouths (the cordon) and, where `doorsLock`, the doors lock (no Enter). A found body holds the scene (rev 4, Motive R4.1; Sky 2026-10-16): a landed report that a person lies there (down, dead, a takedown seen), the body still there and open, or a woken victim's own report where he woke, brings a unit of officers at any Alert (not bound by robot reach; not one of the dial's counted units; at Alert 2 the response unit is it), the level's dispatch after the landing. The scene holds the entrance the body lies at (within values.near-m) and every entrance within witness range of it on a clear line: from an officer's arrival (its check and its `search.s` sweep, opening stashes only at Alert 2 or more) until the unit stands down (the timers below), a held entrance refuses Enter (`door-held`) and any exit through it; an Enter under way finishes and comes out by a door not held (the service door, else the public door), or waits inside while both are held; a cancelled Enter comes out without Vale by the public door, else the service door, or waits inside while both are held (the wait cannot be cancelled; brief 013 E3). A missed check-in is an empty post, no body: it holds nothing. Counts are kept, not repeated: a later alarm tops them up. One incident is one dispatch (brief 013 D, Aster 2026-10-16): the first landed report of an incident dispatches; a later report of it that raises the Alert tops that dispatch up to the new Alert's counts, from the destinations the first set; any other later report of it sends nothing (a unit already out may be sent on to a scene no unit covers). A robot is a patrol unit (weapons.health.patrol, a pistol, trained) walking at `robotSpeed`; the patrol robot is the first robot when it is on its sweep and answers after `robotWire`; the others and the officers start at the site's docks and posts, else at the response unit's entry; they leave one every `launchGap` ticks. Robots and units stop at `cap` combatants (§06). Destinations, in order, duplicates within witness range dropped: the scene; the missing person's post and the stands his lover, family and workmates are meant to be at now, and his car (up to `spread`); the alarm-raiser's ties likewise (up to `spread`); at Alert 3 the mouths. Robots take them in order, the nearest free robot first, ties on id, each only a place within `robotReach` of where it starts (its dock, or the patrol's place on its sweep): farther places are for officers; units go to the scene, then to the place with the fewest units. A unit within witness range of the scene with a clear line verifies: a body there is confirmed (the act's Trail, a kill's Standing, Alert to the confirmed level; the seal starts only on a confirmation at Alert 2 or more, the level's `seal` after the later of the confirmation and the response unit on the street (the seal is the unit's cordon, as for gunfire; Motive rev 3); a knocked-out victim is brought round and gives his statement); no body is unfounded (Alert stays, no seal). Arriving, a unit checks `check`, then robots hold the point (a watcher) and officers search `search.s`: at Alert 2 or more they open every stash within `search.m` of the scene, nearest first, `search.stash` each; a report from a stash itself (a noise, a round) opens that stash at any Alert. Units stand down `standDown.inquiry` after the last alarm at Alert 1 and `standDown.search` at Alert 2, never at Alert 3. The world places report points and the response's origins by rule, so that every walkable cell is within `world.report` of a report point and within `world.dock` of a dock or post (R-REPORT, R-DOCK, checked by the world's tools; the engine reads the places the world exports). Every staff post checks in by voice every `checkIn` from the start of the shift at the post and at its end: a missed mark is a report that lands at the mark at the post. A person who expects a tie at a stop they share (lover, family, workmate; from the people file's routines, never authored) and is at the place without them, while the tie's routine puts them there and the tie is down, held or stashed, raises the alarm after `suspicion.s` (times `suspicion.pm` by temperament, per mille; default a flat 20 s): a missing-person report from where they stand; a turned waiter says nothing; a person being taken reports nothing.

custody.rule: What a capture at Go leaves the campaign (brief 018 §3), worked at the debrief until a campaign layer runs: +trail per captured operative (the campaign's Trail, so Heat); the operative is held at the district's police post (the non-door post nearest the car) and a rescue is offered there for `missions` missions, after which the operative is moved out of reach (Sky 2026-10-18 answer 2: not lost); wounds carry over. At capture an operative left standing takes resentment +abandonedResentment and loyalty −abandonedLoyalty. Once in each between-missions phase while held: fear +fear, loyalty −loyalty, then the Talker test; every value clamped to its scale; talking is once and for good. The founding cell starts at `cellStart`; recruits keep their own scales. A captive who talks gives cell-face for every operative, cell-car, place-time and contact for every turned contact. The debrief projects it: holds = the missions the captive holds before the questioning it talks at.

campaign.rule: What a takedown leaves the campaign, worked out at the mission's end for the debrief (no campaign layer runs yet). A killing never found in the mission is a missing person: missing.trail (no homicide), no Standing, his family, lover and workmate ties fear +missing.tiesFear (worry), the block where he was last seen gets areaWatch.step posted guard and camera for areaWatch.missions missions, and a case opens that stays open until the body is found. A found killing: takedown.trail.kill with the act's Trail, Standing takedown.foundKillStanding on confirmation, his ties grieve (a turned contact takes the saw-violence move, everyone else fear +missing.tiesFear), the area watch as above, and a case that closes after cases.close missions. A knockout hidden or restrained to the end comes home and gives a statement: the act's Trail and his facts as leads; his own fear +1 (resentment +1 if he saw it coming). The district's security level is its base + floor(open cases / cases.perLevel), at most cases.cap above the base.

rounds.rule: A server who works a terrace (brief 022; the baked round sim/data/handover.rounds.json, made by tools/routines from contracts/people/routines.rules.json, Pulse) walks to the tables on a round clock and back to her post; her position is the round's. The round clock stops while she is held: from the tick an order of a verb in `holds` is taken on her to the tick it lands, plus `linger`; an order taken inside the linger extends the same hold; she stands where she is, turned to the operative. Watch holds nothing. The round ends, for the rest of the mission, at the first of `ends` (Alert 2, any shot, a body found, the final fight): she walks back along her own path and stands her post. Called (the summons): the guard walks to a stop at her side, `close` from her post, facing her: the baked stops (rounds file guard.stops: the ring of `close` round her post, free ground, most lateral first, her left first) are read in order and the first with nobody within `clear` of it at the tick of the call is his (the operatives not down and not inside, the patrol, everyone on the street; not her, not him); if every stop is taken, the stop whose nearest person is farthest, the earlier on a tie; a file with no stop keeps the old stop, `close` short of her post on his own route; she breaks off and walks back to her post, they stand together from his arrival to his turn plus `part`, and her round resumes at the start of its next rest. Summon's reach, its refusals and its walk limit read her post, never her pose.
rounds.reason: Motive confirms the numbers; the baked file's rules (lingerS, closeCm, partS, stayS) must equal these and summon.stay, or the engine rejects it.

blastStanding.rule: Brief 096 (Motive, rivals.html §4; engine 0.41.0): a car the cell set burning that explodes with any city person on the street within `near` of it is a menace act whoever was in it: Standing moves by `v`, once a car (beside the existing violence-seen step when a civilian sees it).
blastStanding.reason: Sky's Hero shields civilians: a blast on a street is a menace act.

target.rule: Every car the mission simulates is a target by its own id (car:getaway, car:official, car:rivals; the range has none; the street's parked and passing cars are the host's dressing, not simulated). A car takes `health` (×fight.lab.healthScale in the lab). At or below `disabledAt` (×healthScale) it is disabled: it stops where it is and never drives again, and its occupants get out on their side and act as people do. At 0 it burns: occupants still able get out at once, and `burn` seconds later it explodes: everyone within `blast.m` with a line to the car takes `blast.damage` (×healthScale), the cell included, and anyone held inside takes it whatever the line. Its cover points are gone once it explodes. Costs, all existing: shooting a car is a shooting (gunfire-trail once, alert.gunfire, the response); the car itself takes no hit or down Trail and no Standing step (property); the blast is violence: seen by a civilian, alert.violenceSeen and a Menace step, once a car; each person it hits is hit by the cell (hit-trail, down-trail, a body if they die), an operative it hits costs no Trail. The getaway car disabled fails the mission getaway-lost (every exit is gone). The official car disabled stays where it stopped and the Take there is still possible; its driver gets out; Vale at the car gets out, and is held inside only while the Enforcer seizes him. The rival car disabled: a broken crew leaves on foot (ai.rivalGone unchanged). Hostiles never choose a car as a target. A fire order on the getaway car, or on the official car with Vale at it, takes the always-hold (GoingLoud.Fails: getaway-lost, vale-dead).

car.drive: Where a car may be (brief 023). The site carries a drive grid (sim/data/handover.site.json `drive`, the walk grid's window and cells, made by tools/sim/drive.ts): a cell is drivable when its centre lies on a carriageway (within half a plan road's width of its centreline), in a kerb bay of the civic block, or on a drive (the world's vehicle crossing from a carriageway over a dropped kerb and the pavement to a bay or yard: civic-block drives[], Splice; the Handover's one is service-drive, Apron Road to serviceBay). Pavements, forecourts, yards and squares are not drivable. Every car that moves on the street routes on drivable cells only, by the walk grid's A* (8 neighbours, no corner cutting, ties by cell index, string-pulled on drivable cells): the turned driver's drive to the service bay with Vale in the back (by the carriageway and the drive, never across a pavement; brief 059), the getaway car's Drive between its stands (cell.driveCar), and the rival car between its points (rulebook rivals). A car's place that lies off the drive grid stands at its nearest drivable cell within 6 m (ties: lowest cell); a place with none, or a car's place that no drive reaches from the pickup, rejects the site at load (unknown = reject). A car keeps off the kerb (brief 023, Keel with Pulse): on a carriageway its centre keeps the site's drive.lane (half the city's lane, life.json traffic.laneWidth) from the edge of the drivable ground where it can, on a drive or in a bay it keeps to the middle; the route never runs nearer an edge than its grid cells did (deterministic, sim Grid.CarRoute). Timing is car.pace's: the drive to the service bay runs at its surfaces' pace from Vale-in (car.pickup), then waits parked in the bay (the driver's camera block is retired, brief 059). Parked in the service bay the car faces the site's car.serviceFacing (the bay's long axis, nose away from the drive it came by). The getaway car leaves the street at Go along its exit lane (getaway.exit, held to the carriageway by SX-1); the rival car drives in, drops three, parks, follows, leaves on a tip and comes back (rulebook rivals). A car never drives through a car: a standing car on another car's way out boxes it in (car.box, engine 0.40.0).

footprint.rule: `ahead` (engine 0.37.0, brief 081): this close to the end of its leg, the rival car's stopping ground is cleared of any agent standing on it. A standing car is ground nobody walks through (engine 0.33.1; brief 041, Sky playing 0.2.122: "characters are walking through cars"). Every car the mission simulates (car:getaway, car:official, car:rivals; the range's spawned cars) blocks, while it stands, the walk cells whose centres lie within its footprint (`len` along its heading, `w` across, centred on the car's point) grown by `clear` on every side; while it drives it blocks nothing. It stands at a stand or a bay, at its stops, parked, waiting with Vale, stopped where its driver went down or where it was disabled, and as a wreck. Its heading is the one the host draws: the getaway car its stand's facing, the official car its bay's long axis at the pickup (site car.blockFacing) and car.serviceFacing in the service bay, the rival car its stop's facing (rivals.car.facing), a stopped car the way it was driving. Every walk made while it stands goes round it (the walk grid's A* on the free cells it leaves; the grid's own cells never change): a walk that would end on its ground ends at the free cell nearest that point and steps in from there (a person getting into the car), and a walk from inside it (getting out) starts at the free cell nearest. A move order to its ground ends at that free cell (no step in). When a car comes to stand, whoever stands on its ground steps to the free cell nearest, and a walk in hand that would cross its ground is walked again round it, to the same end, from where the walker is (engine 0.36.0, brief 079; an operative mid-act stays, his act holds him). The response unit's walk, made once at load, goes round the mission's start cars. At the car is within `reach` of its body (no longer at-reach-cm of its centre): Board and a rival reaching Vale at the getaway car. A disabled official car's people stand beside it across its heading, the driver on the road side and Vale on the kerb side. The crowd's routine legs go round the cars standing when each leg sets out (read at the start of the tick): the legs built at load go round the mission's start cars (the getaway car at its first stand, the official car at the pickup); once a car stands elsewhere a leg that would cross it is walked again round the cars standing then.

pickup.rule: Vale's car at the official bay (brief 059 K1–K4; GDD v0.25.0 §07; Sky's answer 3a). Vale always walks from the official door to his car (5:50 to 6:10) and gets in `valeIn` later. Unturned, his driver drives him away then: the mission fails vale-leaves. Turned, the driver drives him round to the service bay along the drive grid at car.pace (car.parks when it stops) and waits there with Vale in the back until the mission's close (schedule.over), whatever his day in the people file says; at the close, if no Take has begun, he drives Vale on and the mission fails vale-leaves. A Take begun before the close holds him until it ends. With no driver (down) the car waits and Vale stands by it. A Take at his car is in-car (no struggle, nothing to witness) only with the driver turned and the car parked round the back; at the front with a turned driver it is refused (driver-brings-vale), and while the car is driving round (car-not-parked). The driver's Call (the camera block) is retired (Motive M059-6.1).

box.rule: Boxed in (engine 0.40.0). A car standing on another car's way out boxes it in. A stand's way out is the drive grid's car route (Grid.CarRoute, the drive's keep-off) from the stand's car cell to the first point of its exit lane (site getaway.stands[].exit, which already starts where the car meets the carriageway), then that lane to its end (fight-block-m): worked out at site load from the site's own data, and a stand whose way out has no route rejects the site (unknown = reject). The official car's way out of the service bay, or of its kerbside stop, is its own route in, backwards, to the carriageway, then fight-block-m on along it. The way out is car.footprint.w wide plus `side` each side, the ground a leaving car sweeps (narrower than the exit lane, which stays the hold's, so a car at the far kerb boxes nothing by accident). A car boxes another when its own footprint (car.footprint len by w at its heading, not grown) meets that ground; the cars that stand are Game.StandingCars() less any car that has exploded, less the leaving car itself: a driving car boxes nothing, a disabled or burning car still stands and still boxes, and the way clears the tick the car in it leaves or explodes. The getaway car boxed in: Go is refused `go` (checked after car-no-driver and before car-held; its ids name the cars in the way, in id order, then any holders) and Drive `drive` (after drive-held); a Drive to a stand whose way out a standing car boxes is refused `into` (after `drive`), naming that car. The official car boxed in: at the pickup its driver waits with Vale aboard and tries again each second; at the close (the turned driver's give-up) he stays, and the verdict is closed-in, cause boxed. At the close, the cell's car boxed in with Vale aboard is closed-in, cause boxed (before car-held). The rival car's legs are no stands and it is never boxed; its blocks are the split's (brief 082, Sky's Q3: later).

box.reason: the physical fact first: no fight on the street moves a car. One rule for every car, from the site's own data, so a generated mission gets the same; the rivals' blocks become plain uses of it when the split is built.

kerb.rule: The kerbside stop (engine 0.40.0). A turned driver who finds his drive taken (the getaway car standing at a stand on it, or driving there) pulls in at the kerb short of it and stops there, nose the way he was driving; the Take, the carry and the close use that stop as they use the bay, and his car never boxes the cell's. Where, worked out at site load for each stand on the drive, from the site's data (site ground.drives[] kerb and polygon, the stand's way out, the driver's car route to the service bay): along his route, the last point before the drive's kerb line at which his footprint grown by `clear` meets neither the drive's polygon nor that stand's way out; moved across, square to his heading, to the kerb the drive joins until the footprint's edge is `edge` off that kerb line; held to the same test. A stand for which no such point exists rejects the site (unknown = reject). At play another standing car there sends him back along his route, a walk cell at a time, until his footprint is clear of it. He decides as he comes up to that point: the drive taken then, he stops there; taken only after he has passed it, he stops where he is (the old stop at the mouth, a tick's window). Logged car.kerbside.

kerb.reason: the old stop across the drive's mouth put his car on the cell's way out once box-in is a rule; at the kerb, 1 m clear of the drive and of the way out, it is outside the pickup camera's reach and clear of the rival car's tail point

lend.rule: The lend and the two cars (engine 0.42.0; Motive L1-L12; 071 R1-R13; read only with `split` 1). L1: a turned driver's car, standing where he stopped for the pickup (the service bay, or his kerbside stop when the drive is taken), with the target inside, becomes a cell car when the in-car Take ends: the Enforcer at the wheel, the target in the back; the driver steps out within the Take and walks off his way (to where the Scout met him, then off the map). L2: each cell car has its own stand, seats, hold, exit lane, box, Go and seen-leaving; Board, Step out and Go name the car (car:getaway, the cell's own, or car:official once lent; a Go or Board that names none is the cell's car); the lent car is never Driven (`refuse.drive`). L3: the lent car seats `seats` standing operative (the Enforcer); another may board it only while no standing operative is aboard (`refuse.board`), to drive it if the Enforcer is down or has stepped out; a carried operative boards with his carrier. L4: its lane is the first fight-block-m of its way out (the service bay's route down the drive and on along Apron Road; from the kerbside stop, straight on), the drive at its polygon, the road at the getaway stand's exit half-width; its police stands are those of the getaway stand nearest it. L5: the win is fixed the tick a cell car leaves with the target aboard (vale.out); the mission runs on. L6: Go on a car is refused while it is boxed in (car.box: its way out), held (a hostile within fight.hold of it or on its lane), gated (the loud fight is at the car with the target: its blocker, picked for the lent car's lane, holds it while up), or with no standing operative aboard; each refusal names the car or the holders. L7: the posted crew springs, besides today's, while the target is in the lent car on an operative standing within fight.safe.ambush of the cell's car, and the tick the lent car leaves. L8: after vale.out, `police` s later (or at the seal, or the close, whichever is first) the mission ends, and every operative not in a car that has left is captured, standing or down (Sky 082.1; the walk-out after the win and split-strand-capture are retired); it ends sooner when no operative is on the map outside a car that has left, and the cell's car leaving after vale.out ends it (no car is left to leave by). Withdraw becomes End. The seal, the close and every operative down no longer fail the mission after vale.out; the cell's car wrecked while the target is lent is no failure. L9: the cell's car still standing when the mission ends is lost: +witness-trail, hunted (debrief car-seen 'left'); the lent car seen leaving is +witness-trail and a lead, not a hunted car. L10: a stand whose car stands on a drive has its rival block point across the drive's mouth: on the carriageway, half a car's length out from the middle of the drive's kerb line, square to it, so the rival car boxes the cell's car on the drive and the official car at its kerbside stop. L11: the lookout's reach is unchanged up to the lent car's Go; in the final fight a rival at a cell car's body with the target in it and no drawn operative standing within cell.reach takes him; after vale.out nobody can. L12: the driver holds the Enforcer's face, the place and the time, never the cell's car.

fight.alwaysRule: The final fight always comes (Sky's S1; Motive briefs/059/motive/s1-rulings.json M059-S1.2 to S1.5; GDD v0.25.0 §06, §07). With safe.always 1: (1) the gate: from the final fight's start until it is over, Go with Vale aboard is refused (car-held) while the fight's blocker is not out (down or gone). The blocker holds the car wherever he stands while he is up, not only on his lane post. Before a blocker is named, whoever is coming holds it: car:rivals while a member still rides in the rival car (the refusal's tick is the first step-out), a member walking back or due to wake (safe), or the officers on their way (loud). The hold within fight.hold or on the exit lane applies on top as always. Go without Vale (withdrawing by car) and the menu's Withdraw are not gated. (2) The late spring: the ambush springs as built (the Enforcer with Vale, not inside, within safe.ambush of the stand's car) or once Vale is in the car; the blocker is picked at the spring from the crew on foot, and if none is on foot then, at the tick the first one steps out, among those on foot (shortest walk, ties by id); each later arrival alerts as he steps out and fires weapons.aimNew after. (3) The floor (safe.floor): at the safe fight's start, count the members able (alive and not bound: a knocked-out one due to wake counts) and coming (on foot, in the rival car, or due back). If fewer than safe.floor, away members come back, the earliest at the stand first (ties by id), until the count reaches the floor or nobody away is left: the tipped car cuts its tip short, re-enters at rivals.car.entry and rides to the stand's rival stop, where the wheelman steps out `out` s later; the warned lookout walks back from rivals.posts.lookoutExit to his spot (rivals.recalled). Nothing spawns; a killed or bound member stays gone. (4) Crew destroyed: with no member able at the fight's start (all killed or bound, none recalled), the safe fight is over at once (rivals.wiped, fight why crew-destroyed) and the gate is open. 0 turns (1), (3) and (4) off: a cell gone before anyone holds the car leaves unfought (engine 0.32.0).
fight.unguarded: Hiding in a held car loses (engine 0.34.0; Motive briefs/067/motive.md §2.3, motive-values.json M067-K3, from BAL-YARD-AT-WILL: the Enforcer downed in the car with Vale at 7:30.0 and the run idle to its end; GDD §06: once Vale is in the car the Enforcer is any operative, and hiding in a held car loses). (a) In the safe fight, with Vale in the getaway car, the car held (a holder stands: Motive's amendment, briefs/067/motive-square.md §4: a free car with the cell aboard waits for Go, and the rivals don't walk to it) and no drawn operative standing outside it (engine 0.35.2, Motive briefs/039/motive/rulings-0.35.1.md §2, Sky's yes 2026-10-27: an operative outside guards the car only drawn, gun out or drawing; an undrawn agent standing by is no guard, so a cell that never draws loses here instead of idling to the close), read as each tick starts (after the last tick's orders, so a Go given as the last Board lands is taken first): the rivals up and not broken, the blocker excepted (he keeps his lane), walk to the car, each to the side of it he comes to, firing as they walk and taking no cover or kite step on the way; the first within car.footprint.reach of its body takes Vale (fail rivals-reach-vale, as today: no drawn operative of the cell stands within cell.reach, engine 0.35.2). A drawn operative standing outside again (pressing F answers it), or the car no longer held, sends them back: each takes cover as an advancing rival does (ai.seek.rival, the Enforcer or the car as the foe). Logged rivals.for-car and rivals.back-to-cover. (b) The cell down: the tick the last operative goes down (in the car or not), the mission fails (cell-down), the fail camera on the shot that downed the last to fall. (c) Go needs a driver: Go is taken only with a standing operative in the car; with only the downed aboard it is refused car-no-driver (any standing operative may give it, from anywhere, once one is aboard). No new timer: the safe fight still ends by the cell's acts, (a), (b), Withdraw, or (loud) the seal. The walk is the fight AI's own movement (an advance to a point), not a routine.

close.rule: The close is a verdict (Motive on Redline E8, brief 080). With Vale in the cell's hands, on foot or in the car, `warn` before the mission's close his absence is noticed: close.warning, once, for the HUD (at once if he is taken later than that). At the close a mission still here fails closed-in, with why: no-driver (nobody aboard can drive; who downed the last of them), car-held (who holds the car), on-foot (Vale still walking; the nearest hostile), no-go (the car free, nobody said go). A Take under way holds the verdict until it ends.

spacing.rule: `cell` (engine 0.37.0, brief 081; proposed, Motive to confirm): an operative's move that would end within `clear` of a claim ends at the free cell nearest it clear of them all, beside the person, not in them. Claims also take the guard, the patrol at rest off its sweep, the waitress and the driver at their places; every response officer spreads the same way as it sets out. Nobody in a fight stands in anybody else (engine 0.36.0; brief 079, Sky: "Rivals were overlapping each other"). Two bodies may pass; where a body's walk ends, or where it stands with none, it claims. The bodies: a final-fight body, a member of the rival crew on foot, the response unit, a police unit, and an operative on the street. A place within the getaway car's Board reach stays within it. A walk that would end within `clear` of another's claim ends at the free walk cell nearest that place clear of every claim, and outside the car's hold and lane unless the place itself was inside (a blocker's lane point stays his; a walk to a car's door ends at the car). A stand or spot found taken this way gives way to that cell, which is the body's stand from then on. A body that stops mid-walk on another's claim takes the step to such a cell, firing as it walks. Officers sent in together from one entry come in file, `file` apart. A claim is read from the walks and stands already in the state, so nothing new is hashed and the same orders give the same places.

fight.holdRule: The hold is entered only on purpose (engine 0.34.0; Motive briefs/067/motive-square.md, motive-values.json M067-SQ1; Pulse's motion): in the final fight a hostile's answer to fire never ends inside the getaway car's hold (`hold` of the car) or on its exit lane: a rival's step out of a shooter's line (the shielding cover, else the nearest free spot within 8 m with no line to him), a rival's step to cover while engaged, a police body's cover or close (fight.kite). If no spot outside serves, it stays where it stands. A walk to a post goes round the hold (the walk grid with the hold's ground closed: the rival crew to its spots, police and the response unit to their stands), unless the post or the walker is already inside it. Exceptions: the blocker (his lane is the road: he comes for the car) and the rivals walking to a held car with nobody outside (fight.unguarded a). An advance on the car or on an operative may enter the hold: that is coming for the car, and it holds. Logged car.held.<how> the first tick each body holds the car at a stand, <how> its reason for being there: blocker, press (for the held car, or the drawn crew for the Vale holder), advance, answer, post (its stand, spot or post, or the way to it); a gate hold by whoever is coming before a blocker is named logs nothing (Waymark's MC-11: no played script logs car.held.answer or car.held.post). Why: only a hostile that comes for the car holds it (MC-11); on the square without its planters the late car's man walked to his ambush spot straight past the car, after the whole cell had boarded a free one, and held it.

kite.rule: Armed hostiles shot at from beyond their reach answer (brief 027 F2, Pulse briefs/027/pulse/kite-response.md with the retest fixes; promoted to today by Sky 2026-10-20, tuning.md §7.9; the lab keeps it on, fight.lab.kite). An operative's shot that lands on an armed hostile marks every living body of the target's side (police: the response unit and the final-fight officers; the brief-013 police units of its dispatch, never robots; rivals: the ambush crew; the pre-fight crew on its own) with the shooter. `react` after the first shot, a body no operative with a weapon out stands inside its effective ring of acts: police close in to the first point of the grid route to the shooter within ai.stopReach of their effective ring, re-planned every `replan`, at most `chase` of walk counted within `contact` of the shooter (a capped body re-arms after `rearm` while the shooter still fires), then hold the cover that shields them within ai.seek.police; a police unit at its scene answers off its post. Police shot at within weapons.lineLapse (3 s), hit or miss, by an operative they have a line to fire back while that shooter is inside their weapon's max ring (every operative who fired on them in that window, not only the last: tuning.md §12.2, engine 0.17.0; the cover below only when they can answer none of them), from where they stand, keeping their cover, at their band's odds (Motive tuning.md §7.10 rule 1; final-fight officers, the response unit, the police units; never robots, the door guard or the patrol). In the final fight, a police body shot from out of its reach takes the cover that shields it, fires back to its max ring, and after `coverHold` with the shooter still out of its max, closes to the shielding cover nearest its stop point of the shooter (within ai.seek.police of it; none: the stop point itself), at a walk, firing as it walks at weapons.mod for its gait (tuning.md §8.3, Sky 2026-10-21; was: nothing while it walks), and plans again each `coverHold` while shots land; unshielded, it plans again `react` after its last plan. It never chases a runner: only a shooter who has fired within `lapse` keeps the alarm. The blocker keeps its lane and answers by the max-ring rule only (§7.10 rule 4, as §7.11.1 narrowed it: the lab's contest officer answers as any police body does). Rivals step out of the line (cover that shields them, else a blind point within 8 m); the pre-fight crew walks out, holds, and walks back `hide` after the last shot on it (its arrival late by the detour), advances to its effective ring of the shooter with no hide, and advances after `hideMax` held. `lapse` with no shot on its side clears the alarm.

lab.rule: EXPERIMENTAL (brief 027 playground; briefs/027/playground.md §2, §3). With the lab on: every health is weapons.health × healthScale; the cell carries the loadout (each weapon's arms within the mission's Arms; the carbine is the cell's), every other gun the lab sidearm; a hit does the weapon's damage (the riot gun nearDamage within near). With pips on, a shot's chance is a step of `chance`: the range band (4 within weapons.pointBlank, 3 within the weapon's eff, 2 within its max), then −1 an untrained shooter and −1 a target still beside cover that shields it (both beyond point blank), −1 a walking shooter, +1 a shooter on a higher level than the target, clamped 1–4; a shooter running toward or across −`runPips` (floor 0), a shooter running away 0 pips whatever the band (tuning.md §8.3); 0 pips is the `pip0` step; a target running this tick past point blank takes weapons.mod.targetRunning on the step's chance; counted by the accumulator (weapons.mod.vale is not read). Aim memory (tuning.md §6.1–6.2; today has it too since §13.1, from acc.start): the count is the pair (shooter, target)'s, for the whole mission and for every shooter (cell, rivals, police, response units): taking a target resumes the count the shooter left on it, and nothing resets it (cease, hold, holster, the draw, an order's end, a volley's end, a walk into range, a switch); a target the shooter has not fired at starts at accStart (today's acc.start is not read). Any switch still waits aimNew (the next shot no sooner than aimNew after taking the target). Off: today's multipliers. Drawing takes `draw`, a new target `aimNew`. Stances `three` (tuning.md §13.4, engine 0.18.0): today's hold, return and free, and a draw sets return. Stances `two` (an option): drawn fires at will (free) or holds (hold); return is refused; a fire order clears hold. `then` free: a fire order whose target is down returns the agent to at will. `close`: a fire order out of range or with no line walks the grid to the nearest free point inside the weapon's effective ring with a clear line (nearest by walk, ties by cell), then fires; it neither lapses nor is refused for range (a driven agent is never walked). Charge (on): each agent holds up to max; a weapon with a charge pays it each shot and does not fire short of it; charge comes back regen a tick once the agent has rested charge.rest since its last charged shot or targeted shot (a volley's shot, any weapon, stamps it; a refund stamps nothing; tuning.md §6.3). A volley {op, target, shots} fires exactly `shots` (1..target.maxShots) at the target at the weapon's cadence, then the agent returns to its stance; it pays the weapon's target charge a shot when given (with charge off: one of target.volleysPerFight a fight), refused no-charge if unpaid, and gets back what it did not fire when it ends early. The field (on): {do: field} pays field.cost, absorbs up to field.absorb damage for field.ticks, and the agent fires nothing while it holds. Police warning (on): an officer, guard, patrol or response unit who sees a drawn weapon before any shot of the run gives policeWarning.ticks to holster: holstered in time, Alert policeWarning.alert, the face is remembered and the watcher logs it (+policeWarning.trail Trail once a shout), no engagement; still drawn, today's drawn-seen (Alert to weapons.costs.drawSeenSecurity, he engages and calls it in). Each watcher shouts at most policeWarning.perWatcher times a mission (tuning.md §6.4): an agent he sees drawn while his shout is open joins it (the same window); once it has closed, the next drawn weapon he sees before any shot is drawn-seen at once. Cameras and rivals never warn. hostilesFireMoving: a final-fight hostile stepping to cover or walking its lane fires as it walks (−1 pip; today's moving modifier with pips off). Panic is allowed outside a fight. kite (on; brief 027 F2, Pulse briefs/027/pulse/kite-response.md; Motive tuning.md §6.6): an operative's shot that lands (hit or miss) on an armed hostile alarms every living body of its side with the shooter (police: the response unit, joined or not, and the final-fight officers; rivals: the ambush crew; the pre-fight crew is its own side; police units: the brief-013 police-n of one dispatch; never the guard, the patrol, civilians or robots). kite.react after the first shot a body acts unless it sees an operative with a weapon out inside its effective ring (by its own sight; it keeps its own fight). Police walk the grid route toward the shooter to the first point within ai.stopReach of their effective ring, re-planned every kite.replan, at most kite.chase of walk a body a run (then the cover that shields it from the shooter within ai.seek.police, held); a holder does not walk home while its alarm is open. The ambush crew takes the cover that shields it from the shooter within ai.seek.rival (once each cover.stepGap), else the nearest free point within 8 m with no line to the shooter; the pre-fight crew walks out to that point, holds, and walks back once kite.hide passes with no shot on it, its arrival clock later by the detour; with no such point it stands. kite.lapse with no shot on its side clears a body's alarm. Retest (brief 027; Suture retest.md R1–R4, Pulse retest-fixes.md, Motive tuning.md §7.2–7.5): the chase budget counts only the walk the answer itself orders while the body is within kite.contact of the shooter (a body's own walk, the walk in, its advance and a blocker's lane never count); a remainder shorter than a grid cell is spent; a spent budget, the alarm still open, re-arms after kite.rearm. A police unit at its scene (check, search, hold) answers as the response unit does, off its post until it walks on. In the final fight no police body chases: shot by an operative it cannot answer, it takes the cover that shields it from him within ai.seek.police and no farther from the car than its stand, and that point becomes its stand; with no such cover it closes to the first point of its route to him within ai.stopReach of its effective ring (keeping the cover it held), and that point becomes its stand (a police unit walks there off its post; Suture retest2.md N1, N4; Pulse reviews the motion). It plans again once where it stands no longer shields it from where he stands now, no sooner than kite.react after its last plan (a shielded body holds; Suture retest3.md N7). The blocker keeps its lane. The pre-fight crew with no hide advances to its effective ring of the shooter (the ambush crew too); out of the line it walks on toward a shooter in its band (beyond its effective ring, within its max) who still fires, once each kite.replan, and leans back out only once no operative with a weapon out stands within its max ring of the lean-out point on a line, else after kite.hideMax it walks on toward him; its advances spend its chase budget. policeContest: in a loud final fight the first n officers take as their stand the first point of the route from their stand to the getaway car within ai.stopReach of their effective ring of it. With the lab on, the pre-fight crew driven back had its hit flag cleared with its health (retired by brief 059: the crew is five people, each down stays down; the crew breaks by rivals.rule). A move never snaps onto a cover point a hostile stands on or walks to. coverSnap (on, B5): a drawn operative's move order to a point on the ground (walk or run; never a move to a named place, a mission point or a person's) whose end lies within coverSnap.snap of a cover point of the site (contracts/world/civic-block.cover.json, present at the mission second, quality at least ai.cover.qPartial) that is free (held by no other body: a hostile that took it or another operative that snapped to it) and joined to the end by a straight walkable line (never through a wall or the cover object) ends on that point instead: the one that shields against the nearest combatant first, then the nearest, then the lower id. The operative holds the point while it walks to it or stands within ai.cover.snap of it; down, inside, in the car or moved off, it lets it go. The shield is still ai.cover's (standing still, inside the point's arc, beyond point blank: −1 pip). A walk into range (close) and a driven agent never snap (stepping out of the car is a move, and does). A holstered operative's move never snaps (a walk on a route stays where it was clicked). The host shows marks within coverSnap.marks of a selected drawn agent; the facing (the nearest combatant) is presentation only.

fight.rule: The final fight (§07 [S]: always; up to 60 s, Sky 2026-10-18; 3–5 hostiles) starts when the Enforcer has Vale. Loud (any shot or Alert ≥ 2): police officers run in from `loud.entry`'s entry (brief 059, Sky's S2: nearest, the response unit's entry or an official entrance of the mission, whichever is the shorter grid walk to the getaway car's stand; response, the response unit's entry), to the stand's police stands, base `loud.officers`, +`loud.alert` if Alert reached 3, +`loud.civilian` if a civilian was shot; the seal clock runs; no allies. Safe (no shots, Alert ≤ 1): the rival crew (rulebook rivals) ambushes the extraction at the getaway car's stand: its hostiles are the crew's own bodies on the roster at the start, never fresh spawns, at most `safe.hostiles`: a member paid off (rivals.turn) is not there, one killed or tied is down (brief 096: each out for good before the fight is one fewer; the −1s are people the cell took out); those posted lurk at their spots, those walking keep their walk, those still in the car come with it to the stand's rival stop and step out (rivals.out, then rivals.step apart) for the stand's spots by role, joining as they step out; a wheelman back from a tip while the fight runs joins it when he steps out (the fight does not wait for him). The ambush springs when the Enforcer brings Vale within `safe.ambush` of the car, or at the cell's first shot at one of them (they lurk in plain sight); a member still in the car springs as he steps out and comes in on his path. With `safe.leaveUnfought` (Sky's S1) a cell gone before the crew reaches its stand leaves unfought; off, a crew member counted in the fight and still on his way (in the car, or walking to his spot before the spring) holds the car. The blocker is picked only from the crew on foot; a helped Inez warns `safe.warn` early (the first volley comes that much later); the guard, if he never saw the cell and was never shot, runs in and fights them (he fires as a guard does). Every hostile drops at `cell.fire.hits` hits. Each hostile fires at its own weapon's cadence (Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md: the volley is retired). The hold (brief 018, Sky 2026-10-18): the car can't leave while a holder stands: a combatant not down, broken or gone within `hold` of the car (any level, line or none) or on the street inside the exit lane, the first `block` of the getaway route's carriageway ahead of the car at the road's width (site getaway.exit, derived from the plan by tools/sim/getaway.ts). An ambusher lying in wait holds only if its spot does. The blocker: `blockers` hostiles per fight go for the road, the one with the shortest grid walk to the lane (safe: an ambusher, moving when the ambush springs; loud: the first officer to arrive, instead of a police stop; ties by id), scored by the grid walk to the post it would take (brief 018 §10, Pulse): the nearest free cover point inside the lane between `blockNear` and `blockFar` of the car point (straight line, as the hold), else the open lane centreline `blockNear` along the lane from its start; it walks there without stopping and holds it as police hold a stand; downed, broken or gone it is not replaced, and a rival blocker breaks with its crew. A rival within `cell.atReach` of the car while Vale is in it, with no operative standing within `cell.reach` of the car, reaches Vale (rivals-reach-vale). The Enforcer down fails the mission only while Vale is not yet in the car. Seen leaving (cell.rule): a final-fight officer sees the car go if it has a clear line to it within weapons.pistol.max.
