block.rule: The block on arrival, on every route (Motive Q4 a). On its timetable, and each time it comes back onto the map, the rival car drives the drive grid to the block point of the stand the cell's car stands at, or is driving to; a Drive of the cell's car started before it stops sends it to the new stand's point. The block point is the stand's own data: the first point of its exit lane at least `standOff` from its car point (on the Handover's square, Rocket Lane 10 m from the bay; on the service drive, the drive's mouth on Apron Road). It stops there; box-in (car.box) does the rest. rivals.out after it stops the three posted step out rivals.step apart for the stand's ambush spots (as before: the seed says who takes which), then the lookout for his post; the wheelman stays at the wheel through the final fight (engine 0.42.0, Motive F1; `wheelmanNear` retired): he gets out only when his car is disabled (`wheelmanOut` after the others, rivals.step apart) or set burning (every rider at once, unhurt: Motive V1), and then fights as any of the crew; in his car he does not fire and is a target only as an operative in a car is (beside cover). Gunfire draws the crew on foot to the Office front (security.rivals.drawn); the car keeps its block. The block ends only when, in the final fight, the crew breaks with the wheelman at the wheel: he drives off at once the way it came, for good, picking nobody up; or when the car explodes (a disabled or burning car still blocks). The crew breaks (Motive F3) when more than half of those in the fight are down (shot, taken down or talked down), counting the posted, the lookout (in it from the spring wherever he is) and anyone misled, not the wheelman at the wheel nor a paid man: 4 on foot break at 3 down, 3 at 2, 2 at 2, 1 at 1. A man who breaks is out of the fight at once (Motive F2): he puts his gun away and runs off by the crew's way off the map at `brokenPace`; he holds no car, is no hostile, is never a target of weapons free and the floor never recalls him; an order can still shoot him, a new shooting at a man running away, traced as any. A man who breaks in the final fight, or whose crew's car is gone, never comes back. A crew that breaks before the final fight with its car still able to drive (engine 0.43.0, Motive's misses page F2) boards it and drives off holstered, out of every fight while away, and comes back to block again security.rivals.retreat after the break (no longer broken once back); at the final fight's start the floor (rivals-floor) may call it back sooner. Destroying the car is what ends them. A crew whose car is destroyed walks off the map and is gone for the mission. Where the rival car boxes the stand in, it is the final fight's block: no body is picked as blocker and the gate (fight.alwaysRule (1)) is the box; Go waits for the car to leave or explode, and for the hold as ever.

lookout.rule: The rival lookout is the cell's job (the turned driver's word, F4, is retired). Posted, he watches the target's car. If he sees it leave its stand with the target aboard, or sees it standing anywhere else with the target aboard, or sees a Take at it, he runs after it at `follow` to where it is (re-aimed each second); on foot within cell act reach of it while the target is in it or being taken, before the final fight, the rivals reach the target (rivals-reach-vale, cause lookout). Seen by his own cone and a clear line (perception.rivals). Three ways to deal with him, the same three for any member on foot (thinning): Mislead (the Scout, cell.mislead: 30 s, +1 T, act reach; the lookout is sent to the target's other door, a posted man to the lookout's post; he watches it `misled` s and walks back; still able, he comes to the final fight from wherever he is, and his card says when he is back), Pay (rivals.turn), or a takedown (rivals.peopleRule). The false tip on the rival car is retired (Motive Q2 a): Mislead names a member on foot, never the car.

turn.rule: The crew are people with a temperament (Motive Q3 a): Mercenary or Loyal, drawn by id alone (not the game's seed: the same five every game, while the seed moves who stands where), no kind over `maxShare` of the crew. They have no need record: Help, Ask and Pressure are not offered on a member. Listen (the Scout, scout.listen's time and reach, private) teaches his temperament; before it the Pay card shows '?'. Pay (the Fixer, `pay` $, `s` s, act reach, private; a member on foot, posted): a Mercenary takes it (+`trail` T) and walks off the map by rivals.posts.lookoutExit, gone for the mission (the floor never recalls a paid man; gone, not down, for the crew's break); a Loyal man refuses, the money stays with the cell, the refusal is remembered (a second Pay is refused) and he tells his crew: at the final fight's spring every member counts the Fixer a foe (ai.intent crewmate). Pay needs a Watch first (`needs` watched, engine 0.43.0; Motive's rivals page pay.needs: 'a Watch first (any agent, as Pay does)'): the crew's timetable read by a Watch on any member or on their car, by any agent; before it the order and its query are refused needs-routine.

rivals.peopleRule: The crew as people (Motive briefs/059/motive/rulings.json M059-3.1, 3.2, 3.4; engine 0.33.0). Takedown (knockout or kill), carry, drop, stash and restrain take a member on foot, never one in the rival car or a final-fight body (fire on him there). He is armed, and aware of the Enforcer by his own facing cone (perception.rivals) and a clear line, without the cone's all-round near ring: aware, the takedown fails and he fires on the Enforcer. A crewmate on foot who sees a takedown on one of the crew (his cone with its near ring, a clear line, inside his weapon's max ring) fires on the taker (ai.intent foe crewmate): the shot is gunfire like any. The body and the act are brief 013's: a civilian who sees the act or finds the body reports it, and its Trail and Alert are charged on a confirmed report as for anyone (knockout hit-trail + down-trail, kill + kill-trail). He is no witness and no reporter, gives no statement, misses no check-in and is never missing: a rival never found costs nothing, between missions too. Knocked out, he wakes after wake-s, staggers stagger-s and rejoins his crew keeping the Enforcer as a foe: the safe final fight as a joiner while it runs; else his post (the lookout his, unless warned off), the Office front while the crew is drawn, the car when the crew has gone back to it, off the map when the car is gone. Tied, he is out until freed: a crewmate on foot within `free` of him unties him in free-s, as a finder does. Before the final fight a crew with more than half of its members on the map down, shot or taken down, breaks (security.rivals.retreat).

beats.rule: A posted body's idle business (Pulse rival-routine.md §5): a loop of {pose, s, yaw}, a pure function of (tick − the tick the post began + the member's phase) mod the loop's length. Position is the post, but the lookout's pace beats walk him lookout-pace-cm along +y and back, linear over the beat. yaw (0, ±30, ±60 degrees) turns the base facing by the integer table cos/sin per mille 30 → (866, 500), 60 → (500, 866), +yaw turning x toward y, divided toward zero. The pose names are the host's (never hashed, no rule reads them); `lean` plays as `watch` unless a cover point lies within cover-snap-cm of the post. The wheelman's loop is for the host's window view while aboard; on foot at a post he plays the posted loop. A loop holds at least minBeats beats and none is longer than maxS seconds (unknown = reject at load).

rivals.rule: The rival crew (brief 059 §2; brief 096, engine 0.41.0: the block on arrival, see `block`, `lookout`, `turn`): five people in one car, rival-1 to rival-3 the posted three, rival-4 the lookout, rival-5 the wheelman, and car:rivals. The car's turn-in is computed back from schedule.rivalsArrive as before (rivals.car.entry, then the old drop's `drop` s and the drive to rivals.park: 2:35 at seed 0, moved by the seed's rivals band); it drives the drive grid at car.pace to the block point (`block`). Before it enters the crew is nowhere on the map. The posted three walk at `speed` to the first `posted` ambush spots of the getaway car's stand, each in id order taking the spot with the shortest grid walk from where he stands (ties the lower spot; the seed may say who takes which), and stand there with their idle business (beats), facing the cell's car. When the getaway car drives to another stand, `follow` s later the three re-plan to that stand's spots and go at `followPace`. The lookout walks to rivals.posts.lookout and watches the target's car (`lookout`). Gunfire draws them as a crew (security.rivals.drawn): on foot they walk to the Office front; the car keeps its block. When the safe final fight starts the members on foot are its bodies, walking to the stand's spots by role (the lookout the 4th, the wheelman the 5th once he is out); the wheelman steps out at the spring. The members are people for Fire (health-rival each, the same gun in the final fight), for the takedown and the body orders (peopleRule), and for Listen, Pay and Mislead (`turn`, `lookout`); in the car they are off the street. Rivals never report, and their moves raise no Alert or Trail. Their cones (perception.rivals) are each member's on foot. Retired by brief 096: the park, the car's tail after the target's car (F2; the lookout on foot follows it now), the false tip on the car (F3), the turned driver's word to the lookout (F4), and the drawn car's stop at the Office front.

investigation.rule: Between the mission and its debrief the city works the Trail (§05 output: findings → debrief Investigation state → next mission). If campaign Trail is at least trail-open, base + perAlert × the mission's Alert investigators each follow `hops` leads. A lead is an incident (an act seen, a shooting, a report: its place, time and witnesses) or a watcher's sighting (§05 watchers: place + time); the newest unfollowed lead goes first. At a lead they question the simulated people who saw it (Sky Q5), nearest first, then by id, one person a hop, each at most once, through investigator.question: a Talker gives every fact they hold and each fact's place-time becomes a lead; a liar gives what people.rules talker.lie says; anyone else, or anyone holding nothing, gives nothing and the hop is spent (K6). A contact questioned is exposed (rulebook exposure). The debrief names the cause: a named witness who gave up the Fixer's face takes precedence over the Trail count (§08).

While the cell does not know the target's temperament (Sky Q3), a line or outcome whose answer differs between the temperaments in the district's band shows '?' (its amount still shows, so the price is always on the card); one that every temperament answers alike shows its answer (Ask in a neutral district reads 'refused', not '?': Motive's review, other findings 3). Commit needs cash for the worst case (base + every line that holds or shows '?'); only lines that hold are charged. Help's `orders` lines change how many Helps turn the person, each order paying the per-order lines. No approach tells the cell the temperament (Sky: only Listen does); a refusal tells it only that this approach is refused by this person, so that card shows refused (✗) from then on (Aster's reading, 2026-10-15).

seed.rule: The seeded start (brief 080). Each new game has a seed, 1 or more, saved with the run; seed + orders replay exactly. Seed 0 (and a script with none) is the neutral start: every draw below at the middle of its band. Each draw is keyed seed/character/stage (streams: one stage, one key) and scaled by the character's fuzziness (fuzz, per mille of the band; 0 = always the same). Drawn once, before the first tick, then fixed for the whole game, so whatever a Watch shows holds: each civilian's routine earlier or later by up to crowd.phase and their pace within crowd.pace (who keeps a post or a server's round keeps its clock: crowd.staffFixed); the rival car's whole timetable by up to rivals.arrive; which rival takes which post round the car; where the patrol begins its sweep, anywhere on it (fair: none of the cell's stands in its cone for fair.firstS, in up to fair.tries draws, else the neutral place); each camera desk's scan phase and each service round's phase. Never by the seed: Vale's shift and the mission's clock, the door guard's marks, places, cast, needs, secrets, prices, the purse. During play only shots draw (weapons.sheet).

how: the subject is one fight. The final fight is one fight, from its first shot by or at the cell to its end (fight over: every hostile down, broken or gone) or the mission's. Outside it, a fight starts at the first shot by or at the cell and ends `quiet` after the last such shot (the crowd's own 'it's over', crowd.quiet). Gunfire still open (its last shot less than `quiet` before) when the final fight starts is the final fight. A fight still open when the mission ends ends with it

public: a person of the city who is not security (one of the city's people who is not a guard, a patrol officer, an investigator or a watcher; the cast by role included, Vale in the Enforcer's hands not) stands on the street within `m` of the shooter of any of the fight's shots, line or no line (the reach that startles the crowd, crowd.scatter). Outside the final fight a fight's shots are those by or at the cell; in it, every shot. A fight nobody heard moves nothing

it moves Standing once, when it ends, by the first outcome that holds; `none` moves nothing (rivals not feared who fired first, feared rivals not driven off, a withdrawal). fired-on: the cell fired, in this fight, on security (the guard, the patrol, the response's officers and robots, the final fight's officers) or on rivals (the rival crew, the final fight's ambush). rivals-public: the mission's rivals as the public sees them (site rivals.public, else fight.rivalsPublic). fired-first: the fight's first shot between the cell and the rivals was the cell's. rivals-broken: every rival body the cell fought in this fight (fired on or was fired on by; in the final fight, every rival of the ambush too) broke, was driven back or is down when it ends

untraced shots count: Standing is the public's judgement, not evidence (fight.traced keeps the final fight's shots out of Trail and Alert only). A shot at a civilian is still violence (witness.sees, seen-violence) on top of the fight's move. A shot at anyone else (the guard, the rivals, officers) seen by a civilian keeps its witness Trail and Alert (violence seen: alert.violenceSeen) but no Standing of its own: its incident is traceable gunfire, and the fight judges it. A drawn weapon seen is still its own incident

events.src: Sky 2026-10-16 ('if you help in a good way then can move to hero'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rules 2 and 3 (approved by Sky, 'sure', 2026-10-16)
how: done-to reads this mission's acts on the subject: helped, a Help order landed on them (memory help, any outcome); pressured, a Pressure landed (memory pressure); knocked-out, an Enforcer's knockout landed (a takedown ko, not a Take, not a kill). Alive: not killed by a takedown that landed (so not missing either) and not shot down (the engine does not tell the wounded from the dead)
outcomes in order, so a person both helped and pressured or knocked out counts as harmed

the step goes to the district where the act was done, once per person however many ties (standing.word.ties) they have; the district's net word is clamped to ±cap after every subject is counted (order-free)
a feeling, not a fact: nobody's memory changes, no fact is told, nothing reaches the investigators; word-quiet-loyalty does not apply (it hides facts)
a contact the Fixer has sealed would not tell (briefs/014/motive-standing.md 'who doesn't'): the rulebook has no such verb yet, so nobody is sealed
events.reason: Sky 2026-10-16: turning conversations are private, which left nothing moving the city toward Hero; Motive's rule lets kindness (and harm, symmetrically) spread one hop through the person it was done to.

events.src: Sky 2026-10-16 (approved Motive's 'the benefit of the doubt'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rule 5
how: per district, last in the phase so it sees every move: standing-moved holds when an act seen or found (in the mission, or a killing found after it: bodies.surface) or any word (standing.word, even one that nets to 0) touched the district this mission
drift-standing moves the district at most `step` toward `to`, never past it: nothing at the start
both outcomes write the district's one Standing line (debrief.lines.standing) with its cause from standing.causes
events.reason: Motive: what the city stops seeing, it forgives; symmetric, so unkept Hero fades back to +2 as Menace does. Last in the phase (Motive had it after standing.word) so that a killing found between missions counts as a move.
